# Pipeline code review, 2026-08-03

Max-effort multi-agent review of `pipeline/` (training, eval, domains, configs,
tests) plus the uncommitted working-tree changes. 6 finder agents across
independent angles, 63 verifier agents, 76 candidates raised, 8 refuted, 68
verified and consolidated into 15 findings.

This document is the input to a fix plan. No fixes have been applied.

**Provenance note.** Every claim below carries a CONFIRMED verdict from an
independent verifier that read the code. Numeric claims attributed to
measurement (median answer calls per rollout, the 4-of-100 e27 episodes, the
identical over/underthinking rates under halved token counts) come from those
agents' own runs against the artifacts on disk. They have not been
independently re-derived here. Everything structural (what the code does, which
branch runs when) is directly checkable in the cited lines.

## Verdict

The pipeline is not fine. The dominant failure mode is the same one that
voided e9-e25: a path computes a plausible number from the wrong quantity and
nothing raises.

Three findings change what the numbers already on disk mean. Four more will
change what the next run means. The rest are robustness and cleanup.

The single most important consequence: **the browsergym eval loop measures the
policy under a different token budget and a different context than training
produced.** e27 is the E1 baseline that e28/e29 are paired against and that the
whole RQ1 claim rests on.

---

## Tier 1: affects numbers already on disk

### 1.1 reasoning_gym `answer` has no done-guard; training scores the last
answer, eval scores the first

`pipeline/domains/reasoning_gym/adapter.py:66-80`

Every other adapter guards re-entry after termination (`textarena:69`,
`finqa:161`, `repl:78`, `browsergym:94`). `ReasoningGymEnvAdapter.answer` does
not: it calls `self._client.step(...)` unconditionally and overwrites
`self.reward` on line 78.

Compounding it, `grpo_runner.py:125-127` sets `max_tool_calling_iterations`
only when `env_config.max_turns > 0`, and no reasoning_gym config sets
`max_turns` (checked across e5, e6, e9-e25 and the probes). TRL's tool loop
therefore runs at its `sys.maxsize` default, which is exactly the failure
CLAUDE.md warns about.

A rollout that answers correctly, reads the tool result, then answers again
and gets it wrong ends with `env.reward = 0.0`. `EnvReward` and
`CosineLengthReward`'s correctness gate (`cosine_length.py:75-78`) train it as
wrong; `agentic_eval._parse_answer` takes the first call and scores it correct.
Measured median: 2.25 answer calls per rollout across e24/e25.

The unbounded loop is also a mechanism for rollouts running to the completion
cap, which is the phenomenon the entire e22/e23 cap-probe line was built to
explain. Worth revisiting that conclusion.

### 1.2 Eval applies `max_new_tokens` per turn, training applies it per
trajectory

`pipeline/eval/agentic_eval.py:397` (also `configs/e26-...:52`)

e27/e28/e29 set `max_new_tokens: 4096` and `max_turns: 8`. Training caps the
whole trajectory at 4096 via TRL's `max_completion_length`. `_run_multiturn_episodes`
calls `model.generate(max_new_tokens=4096)` once per turn with no running total,
so an eval episode can generate up to 32768 tokens.

4 of e27's 100 held-out episodes score correct only because they received about
1.8x the trained budget. `mean_token_count` is summed over a budget regime the
policy never trained under, and `hit_generation_cap` can never fire for the
trajectory-level cap that actually bound training.

### 1.3 Multi-turn eval discards the model's own reasoning between turns

`pipeline/eval/agentic_eval.py:203` (test at `tests/test_multiturn_eval.py:100`
encodes the current behaviour)

`gen_turn` decodes the completion, extracts `(name, args, n_tokens)`, throws
the text away, and the loop appends an assistant message with
`{"content": ""}` plus a tool_calls stub.

Training keeps the full generated text in the running completion.
`browsergym_difficulty_correction.md` says so explicitly ("about 1030 tokens
per turn on click-checkboxes-large, with every prior turn's block retained in
the completion"), and that retention is why the 4096 ceiling binds at all.

At eval the model enters turn 2 having lost its own turn-1 think block, which
for Qwen3 is roughly 300 to 1000 tokens of the reasoning that selected the
element id. Every multi-turn eval number measures a policy with amnesia between
turns. The divergence is invisible because both paths report identical per-turn
`n_tokens`.

### Scope note for 1.2 and 1.3

Both defects apply uniformly to every arm evaluated by this loop. A paired
e27-vs-e28 comparison where both arms ran the same buggy eval is not
automatically invalid, because the bias is shared. What is invalid is any
absolute claim, and any comparison against a number produced by a different
eval version. **Fixing the eval loop obliges a re-eval of e27**, or the pairing
breaks.

---

## Tier 2: will corrupt the next run

### 2.1 The uncommitted untagged-JSON parser relabels truncated completions as
clean terminations

`pipeline/eval/agentic_eval.py:55-64`

A Qwen3 rollout that fills the budget and is cut after the closing brace of its
answer JSON but before `</tool_call>`: `_TOOL_CALL_RE` requires the closing tag
so it finds nothing, `tagged` stays False, and the unanchored `raw_decode` scan
then finds the complete object and yields it. `_parse_answer` returns an
answer, so `_run_episodes` sets `terminated=True`, `stop_reason="env_done"`
(lines 154-155) for an episode that hit the cap. Before this change the same
episode was `terminated=False`, `stop_reason="hit_generation_cap"`.

Same for any JSON object with a `"name"` key inside a `<think>` block or a
markdown fence when the real call never landed.

Net: non-termination rate drops, accuracy rises, the `hit_generation_cap`
bucket empties. That is the one distinction CLAUDE.md and `metrics.py:31-33`
say must never be collapsed, and it is what made e9-e21 uninterpretable.
Re-running eval on any existing Qwen checkpoint now produces different,
better-looking numbers with no marker that the parser changed.
`tests/test_agentic_episode_eval.py:84` only covers the case where a tagged
call is present, so this path is untested.

This is uncommitted, so nothing on disk is affected yet. Fix before the next
eval.

### 2.2 The cosine reward measures length with two different rulers on the two
sides of its own correctness gate

`pipeline/training/rewards/cosine_length.py:87,103`

`_n_tokens` uses `len(completion_ids_i)` (raw ids, including `<think>`,
`<tool_call>` and `<|im_end|>` framing) when `_is_multiturn` is False, and
`model_token_count` otherwise. `model_token_count` re-encodes only `content` +
`reasoning_content` + `json.dumps(arguments)` and drops all framing
(`utils.py:53-66`).

`_is_multiturn` is True exactly when TRL interleaved a `role == "tool"`
message, i.e. exactly when the model actually called a tool. So the branch is a
proxy for the correctness gate: rollouts that answered are counted one way,
rollouts that never answered (always scored wrong) are counted the other and
carry every framing token. The wrong arm is inflated by tens of tokens purely
by measurement.

Because `AdvantageWeightedComposer` z-scores per prompt-group, that constant
offset between the two subsets shifts every rollout's normalised cosine value.
Part of the correct-vs-wrong length structure the reward trains on is an
artifact of which counter ran.

Same class as the `reasoning_content` bug.

### 2.3 `--seeds` shifts the dataset seed base by 1, so replicates share ~99%
of their data

`pipeline/training/train.py:195`

`training.batch --seeds 42 43 44` materializes three configs differing only in
the top-level `seed` (`batch.py:80`). That scalar goes straight through as
`seed_base` to `build_seed_dataset`, which mints `seed..seed+size-1`. At
`size: 500` the three runs share 499, 498 and 499 of 500 training questions.
`run_agentic_eval` sets `seed_base = seed + 100000` (`agentic_eval.py:363`), so
the three eval sets share 99, 98 and 99 of 100 questions, and eval is greedy so
shared questions decode identically.

The replicates vary the optimizer RNG and nothing else. Pooling them (as the
poly seed-43 replication did) counts the same questions up to three times and
reports a CI far tighter than the data supports.

Fix: `seed_base = seed * size`, or an explicit disjoint offset.

### 2.4 Over/underthinking rates use a per-run percentile threshold, so they
cannot detect compression

`pipeline/eval/metrics.py:160`

Verified numerically: 100 samples at mean 1146 tokens, and the same samples
with every `n_tokens` halved, both return `overthinking_rate 0.2424` and
`underthinking_rate 0.0909`. Bit-identical, because the P75/P10 threshold moves
with the distribution.

`agentic_eval.py:424` calls `compute_metrics(results)` with no threshold
overrides, and `load_reference_thresholds` (`metrics.py:358`), the function
that exists to pin a fixed cross-run threshold, has zero callers anywhere.

So `eval_report.md` prints an overthinking rate per arm that cannot detect the
compression E2 exists to produce, and a reader comparing two arms is comparing
two different thresholds.

### 2.5 The entropy reward conditions on a prompt missing the tool schema

`pipeline/training/rewards/token_entropy.py:77`

Every rollout prompt in this pipeline is rendered with the adapter's tool spec
injected. `_prompt_to_text` calls `apply_chat_template` with no `tools=`
argument, then concatenates `prompt_ids + completion_ids` and slices logits at
`[p_len-1 .. p_len+c_len-2]`. The forwarded sequence is one the policy never
generated from: hundreds of tokens of tool-schema context are absent. H_t is
the entropy of the completion given a truncated context.

e19 (the only entropy arm) reported null-to-harmful on this quantity.

Worse in multi-turn: `comp_ids` comes from `kwargs['completion_ids']`, which
`CosineLengthReward._is_multiturn` documents as including injected tool-result
tokens, so entropy would average over text the env wrote. The cosine reward
guards against exactly that; this one does not.

---

## Tier 3: operational and robustness

### 3.1 `--base-model` writes into the trained run's output directory

`pipeline/eval/runner.py:51`

The deleted `run_eval(baseline=True)` path routed base-model artifacts to
`runs/_baselines/<slug>/` (surviving artifacts: `pipeline/runs/_baselines/qwen3-1.7b/`,
`.../qwen-7b/`). Commit `e1f1cdf` deleted `run_eval`; commit `37f9b74` re-added
the condition as `--base-model` but resolves `run_dir = os.path.join("runs", exp_id)`
unconditionally.

`python -m eval.runner --config configs/e27-... --base-model` overwrites e27's
`eval_report.json`, `eval_report.md`, `episodes_held_out.jsonl` and
`episodes_shifted.jsonl` with untrained-model numbers. No backup, no warning.
The only mitigation in the repo is a prose note in RUNNING.md's Traps section.

(`e0b-browsergym-base-llama3_2-1b.yaml` has its own `experiment_id`, so it is
not affected. The hazard is running `--base-model` against a trained run's
config.)

### 3.2 `_is_real_report` checks a `smoke` key nothing ever writes

`pipeline/training/batch.py:176`

`_is_real_report` returns False only for `status in (skipped, error)` or a
truthy `smoke` key. `run_agentic_eval` writes its report
(`agentic_eval.py:428-441`) with keys experiment_id / model_slug / seed /
compose_method / mode / checkpoint / results. No `status`, no `smoke`.

So a `--smoke` batch leaves a 4-episode report classified as real, and the
follow-up unattended `--train --eval` prints `skip: eval_report.json exists`
and never runs the 100-episode eval. The 4-episode numbers flow into
`eval.plots` and any comparison table.

The train side does have a marker (`train.py:204-205` writes
`checkpoint-final/.smoke`). `tests/test_batch_skips.py:14-16` passes only
because it hand-builds a `{"smoke": True}` dict the production writer never
produces.

### 3.3 The `.smoke` marker is never cleared, bricking the run for the batch
runner

`pipeline/training/train.py:205`

`save_lora` calls `save_pretrained`, which does not clear the directory, and
`--overwrite` only bypasses the FileExistsError without deleting anything.

After a smoke batch: `checkpoint-final/.smoke` is permanent. Next
`training.batch cfg --train --eval` without `--force`: `_is_real_checkpoint`
returns False so train is not skipped, `_run_train_phase` omits `--overwrite`
because `force` is False, `train.py:151-155` sees `checkpoint-final/` and
raises FileExistsError. Both attempts burn, eval is skipped, `_write_eval_stub`
declines because the stale smoke report is there. The run is unrunnable through
the batch runner without `--force`, and what is left on disk is a 3-step
checkpoint plus a 4-episode report under a real experiment_id.

### 3.4 `validate_config` has no whitelist for `training` keys

`pipeline/training/config_schema.py:270`

The file closes the silent-passthrough gap for top level, rewards, eval and
`training.env_config` (that last one added specifically to catch `datsaet`).
There is no equivalent set for the keys of `training` itself.

`max_prompt_lenght: 6144` in a max_seq 8192 config passes validation, is
ignored, and `_grpo_config` falls back to `max_seq // 2` = 4096, so
`max_completion_length` becomes 4096 instead of 2048. The run trains at a
geometry its own config and description contradict, and the frozen
`runs/<exp>/config.yaml` records the typo rather than the value used.

Same silent fallback for `n_rollouts` (the GRPO group size, hence the advantage
denominator), `micro_batch_size`, `kl_beta`, `save_steps`.

Worth grepping every existing config against the real key set before trusting
any frozen geometry.

### 3.5 `plots.load_report` raises on every multi-split report

`pipeline/eval/plots.py:72`, `:250`

With `split_name=None`, line 72 evaluates
`_SPLIT if _SPLIT in results or len(results) != 1 else next(iter(results))`.
e27/e28/e29 declare `held_out` and `shifted`, so `"agentic" in results` is
False but `len(results) != 1` is True, leaving `wanted = "agentic"`, and line
74 raises.

`make_figures` calls `load_report(p)` positionally and `main()` defines no
`--split`, so the parameter is unreachable from the CLI. No figure can be
produced for the browsergym campaign, and a mixed glob dies after the first
browsergym entry, losing the figures that would have worked.

### 3.6 Only `TypeError` is caught around tool dispatch

`pipeline/eval/agentic_eval.py:197`

`_run_multiturn_episodes` wraps `getattr(env, name)(**(args or {}))` in
`except TypeError` only. An HTTP error from the env server, a
`ConnectionResetError` or a pydantic validation error propagates out of the
loop, past `finally: server.stop()`, and kills the process before
`_write_episodes` runs. `_write_episodes` is called only after the whole split
finishes, so a hiccup on episode 95 of 100 destroys all 95 trajectories and
writes no jsonl at all.

That contradicts the file's own durability rationale at lines 256-261, and
costs several GPU-hours per occurrence on the e27/e28/e29 geometry.

Secondary defect in the same handler: on a caught `TypeError`,
`calls.append(name)` still runs (line 201), so a call that never reached the
env counts toward `n_steps` and inflates `mean_verification_depth` in the RQ2
panel.

---

## Checked and refuted

Eight candidates were raised and killed by verification. Recorded so they are
not re-litigated:

- `compose.py:23,24` - two separate claims that per-prompt-group z-scoring
  groups incorrectly because seed rows share a prompt. Refuted.
- `agentic_eval.py:55` - that the untagged scan attempting a decode at every
  `{` is itself the defect. Refuted (the real defect is 2.1, the relabelling).
- `utils.py:12` - that `extract_content` still ignores `reasoning_content`.
  Refuted; `model_token_count` is the path that matters and it was fixed.
- `finqa/adapter.py:114` - that local csv re-read desyncs from the server's
  shuffle. Refuted.
- `textarena/adapter.py:75` - reward/done read off `result.observation`.
  Refuted.
- `agentic_eval.py:34` - that scoring the two lineages by different rules
  confounds e0b. Refuted.
- `grpo_runner.py:77` - that `training.max_prompt_length` is never forwarded to
  `GRPOConfig`. Refuted.

## Not included

The remaining verified-but-omitted findings are dead code, doc drift, and one
latent NaN path in `compose.py` (unbiased `std()` returns NaN for a
single-element group and the `std < 1e-6` guard cannot catch it, because every
comparison against NaN is False). TRL currently absorbs it; it becomes live if
a group of size 1 ever reaches the composer.

---

## Suggested fix order

Ordered by what unblocks the most work, not by severity:

1. **2.1** (parser relabelling) - uncommitted, cheapest, and blocks every
   future eval.
2. **1.2 + 1.3** (eval budget and context) - then re-eval e27. Nothing in the
   browsergym campaign can be compared across an eval-code change otherwise.
3. **3.1** (`--base-model` clobber) - one line, prevents losing e27.
4. **1.1** (done-guard + turn cap) - required before any further reasoning_gym
   run.
5. **2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5** - correctness of the measurements the thesis reports.
6. **3.2 through 3.6** - operational, do in one cleanup pass.

4	episodes (seeds disjoint from training), parses each tool call, scores it via
5	the env, and reports success rate + token-efficiency metrics.
6	"""
7	import json
8	import os
9	import re
10	import sys
11	
12	from domains.env_base import CORRECT_REWARD_THRESHOLD
13	from eval.metrics import SampleResult, compute_metrics

15	# The model answers by emitting a Hermes-style tool call (Qwen3 native format):
16	#   <tool_call>{"name": "answer", "arguments": {"answer": "42"}}</tool_call>
17	_TOOL_CALL_RE = re.compile(r"<tool_call>\s*(\{.*?\})\s*</tool_call>", re.DOTALL)
18

20	def _iter_tool_payloads(text: str):
21	    """Yield each tool-call payload dict the model emitted, in order.
22	
23	    Two wire formats, because the study runs two model lineages. Qwen3 wraps
24	    calls in Hermes `<tool_call>` tags; Llama 3.x emits a bare JSON object with
25	    no tags at all. Tagged matches take priority and short-circuit the rest, so
26	    a model that emits tags is parsed exactly as it was before this existed and
27	    the untagged scan only runs when there were none to find.
28	
29	    Training does not need this - TRL's `parse_response` normalises both from
30	    the token ids. Eval parses the decoded text itself, so it has to agree.
31	
32	    One deliberate difference from TRL: its `llama3_schema` regex is anchored at
33	    `^`, so a call preceded by prose is training-invisible and never executed.
34	    The scan below is unanchored, which matches how the Hermes branch has always
35	    treated Qwen (`finditer` over the whole completion) and keeps the two
36	    lineages scored by one rule. It does mean eval credits a prose-prefixed call
37	    that training would have dropped - relevant mainly to the untrained E0 arms,
38	    which have not yet learnt to lead with the call.
39	    """
40	    tagged = False
41	    for m in _TOOL_CALL_RE.finditer(text):
42	        try:
43	            payload = json.loads(m.group(1))
44	        except (ValueError, TypeError):
45	            continue
46	        if isinstance(payload, dict):
47	            tagged = True
48	            yield payload
49	    if tagged:
50	        return
51	
52	    # Untagged JSON can start anywhere in the completion, and a brace-matching
53	    # regex gets this wrong on nested objects. `raw_decode` from each `{` is the
54	    # stdlib's own scanner, so it stops at the right brace by construction.
55	    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
56	    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
57	        if ch != "{":

60	            payload, _ = decoder.raw_decode(text, i)
61	        except ValueError:

70	    Qwen/Hermes calls it `arguments`, Llama 3.x calls it `parameters`. A payload

183	        messages = list(make_messages(obs))
184	        total_tokens = 0
185	        calls = []

191	            total_tokens += int(n_tok)
192	            if name not in tool_names:
193	                stop_reason = _no_call_reason(n_tok, gen_cap)
194	                break
195	            try:
196	                feedback = getattr(env, name)(**(args or {}))
197	            except TypeError as e:
198	                # Malformed model arguments (wrong/extra kwargs) become feedback
199	                # rather than crashing the episode.
200	                feedback = f"Tool call error: {e}"
201	            calls.append(name)
202	            messages.append({
203	                "role": "assistant", "content": "",
204	                "tool_calls": [{"type": "function",
205	                                "function": {"name": name, "arguments": args or {}}}],
206	            })
207	            messages.append({"role": "tool", "content": str(feedback)})
208	            if getattr(env, "done", False):
209	                stop_reason = "env_done"
210	                break
211	        r = float(env.reward)
212	        results.append(SampleResult(
213	            correct=r >= CORRECT_REWARD_THRESHOLD,
214	            n_tokens=total_tokens, n_steps=len(calls), reward=r,
215	            terminated=stop_reason == "env_done",
216	            stop_reason=stop_reason, tool_calls=calls,
217	        ))

301	def run_agentic_eval(config, checkpoint_dir, domain, run_dir, n_episodes=None) -> dict:
302	    """Evaluate a trained agentic policy over held-out env episodes.
303	
304	    Loads the LoRA checkpoint, launches the OpenEnv server (no Docker), runs
305	    greedy tool-calling episodes per split, scores via the env, and writes
306	    runs/<exp>/eval_report.json + .md keyed by split name.
307	
308	    `checkpoint_dir=None` evaluates the base model with no adapter - reward
309	    condition E0. The rest of the path is identical, so E0 is measured through
310	    exactly the same episode loop, prompt framing and scoring as every trained
311	    arm; a separately written probe script would not be.
312	    """
313	    import torch
314	    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, BitsAndBytesConfig
315	    from peft import PeftModel
316	
317	    from training.registry import get_model_config
318	    from training.env_server import build_env_server
319	
320	    model_cfg = get_model_config(config["model"]["slug"])
321	    load_4bit = config["model"].get("load_in_4bit", model_cfg["load_in_4bit"])
322	    dtype = torch.bfloat16 if torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() else torch.float16
323	    quant_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
324	        load_in_4bit=True,
325	        bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
326	        bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
327	        bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=dtype,
328	    ) if load_4bit else None
329	
330	    # Native tool-calling template (do NOT apply the reasoning-tag template).
331	    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_cfg["model_name"])
332	    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
333	        model_cfg["model_name"], quantization_config=quant_config,
334	        torch_dtype=dtype, device_map="auto",
335	    )
336	    if checkpoint_dir is None:
337	        print("No checkpoint: evaluating the base model (E0)")
338	    else:
339	        print(f"Loading checkpoint: {checkpoint_dir}")
340	        model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, checkpoint_dir)
341	    model.eval()
342	
343	    eval_cfg = config.get("eval", {}) or {}
344	    agentic_cfg = eval_cfg.get("agentic", {}) or {}
345	    base_n = int(n_episodes if n_episodes is not None else agentic_cfg.get("n_episodes", 100))
346	    max_new = _completion_budget(config, model_cfg["max_seq_length"])
347	    do_sample = bool(eval_cfg.get("do_sample", False))
348	    seed = int(config.get("seed", 42))
349	    splits = _resolve_splits(config, base_n)
350	
351	    # Created up front: each split writes its episode records as it finishes, so
352	    # a crash in a later split does not lose the earlier one's trajectories.
353	    os.makedirs(run_dir, exist_ok=True)
354	    split_metrics = {}
355	    for split in splits:
356	        n = split["n_episodes"]
357	        if config.get("_smoke"):
358	            # A multi-turn agentic eval runs n * up-to-max_turns model.generate
359	            # calls, so keep the smoke episode count small - it only checks that
360	            # the eval loop runs.
361	            n = min(n, 4)
362	        env_config = split["env_config"]
363	        seed_base = seed + split["seed_offset"]
364	        # One server per split: server_env is derived from env_config (task id,
365	        # turn cap, data path), so a split that changes it needs its own process.
366	        split_config = {**config,
367	                        "training": {**config["training"], "env_config": env_config}}
368	        server = build_env_server(split_config, domain, python=sys.executable)
369	        server.start()
370	        server.wait_until_ready()
371	        if server.repo_envs_path not in sys.path:
372	            sys.path.insert(0, server.repo_envs_path)
373	        try:
374	            env = domain.make_env_factory(server.base_url, env_config)()
375	            tools = domain.eval_tools(env)
376	
377	            def gen_fn(question):
378	                messages = domain.episode_messages(question)
379	                enc = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
380	                    messages, tools=tools, add_generation_prompt=True,
381	                    return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True,
382	                ).to(model.device)
383	                plen = enc["input_ids"].shape[1]
384	                with torch.no_grad():
385	                    out = model.generate(**enc, max_new_tokens=max_new, do_sample=do_sample)
386	                comp_ids = out[0][plen:]
387	                text = tokenizer.decode(comp_ids, skip_special_tokens=False)
388	                return _parse_answer(text), int(comp_ids.shape[0])
389	
390	            def gen_turn(messages):
391	                enc = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
392	                    messages, tools=tools, add_generation_prompt=True,
393	                    return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True,
394	                ).to(model.device)
395	                plen = enc["input_ids"].shape[1]
396	                with torch.no_grad():
397	                    out = model.generate(**enc, max_new_tokens=max_new, do_sample=do_sample)
398	                comp_ids = out[0][plen:]
399	                text = tokenizer.decode(comp_ids, skip_special_tokens=False)
400	                parsed = _parse_tool_call(text)
401	                if parsed is None:
402	                    return None, None, int(comp_ids.shape[0])
403	                name, call_args = parsed
404	                return name, call_args, int(comp_ids.shape[0])
405	
406	            print(f"Agentic eval [{split['name']}]: {n} episodes "
407	                  f"(seed_base={seed_base}, max_new_tokens={max_new})")
408	            if getattr(domain, "multi_turn", False):
409	                # env_config.max_turns is the single turn cap - training passes it
410	                # to TRL as max_tool_calling_iterations and each domain maps it to
411	                # its server's own cap var, so eval must read the same key or it
412	                # measures a different episode length than training produced.
413	                max_turns = int(env_config.get("max_turns", 8))
414	                results = _run_multiturn_episodes(
415	                    env, n, seed_base, gen_turn,
416	                    max_turns=max_turns, make_messages=domain.episode_messages,
417	                    tool_names={t.__name__ for t in tools}, gen_cap=max_new,
418	                )
419	            else:
420	                results = _run_episodes(env, n, seed_base, gen_fn, gen_cap=max_new)
421	        finally:
422	            server.stop()

424	        split_metrics[split["name"]] = compute_metrics(results)
425	        _write_episodes(results, seed_base,
426	                        os.path.join(run_dir, f"episodes_{split['name']}.jsonl"))
427	
428	    report = {
429	        "experiment_id": config.get("experiment_id"),
430	        "model_slug": (config.get("model") or {}).get("slug"),
431	        "seed": config.get("seed", 42),
432	        "compose_method": (config.get("rewards") or {}).get("compose_method", "advantage_weighted"),
433	        "mode": "agentic",
434	        # E0 (no adapter) is a first-class condition, so the report says which
435	        # policy produced it rather than leaving it to the experiment_id.
436	        "checkpoint": checkpoint_dir,
437	        "results": {name: _metrics_to_dict(m) for name, m in split_metrics.items()},
438	    }
439	    json_path = os.path.join(run_dir, "eval_report.json")
440	    with open(json_path, "w") as f:
441	        json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
442	    with open(os.path.join(run_dir, "eval_report.md"), "w") as f:
443	        f.write(_report_md(report["experiment_id"], split_metrics))
444	    summary = ", ".join(f"{name} {m.accuracy:.3f} (n={m.n_samples})"
445	                        for name, m in split_metrics.items())
446	    print(f"Agentic eval report written to {json_path} [{summary}]")
447	    return report

450	def _report_md(experiment_id, split_metrics: dict) -> str:
451	    """Human-readable report: one block per split.
452	
453	    The three dimensions the protocol interprets jointly (task success, the
454	    targeted efficiency, the off-target panel) sit in one block per split so a
455	    drop in one is read next to a gain in another, not on a separate page.
456	    """
457	    out = [f"# Agentic eval: {experiment_id}\n"]
458	    for name, m in split_metrics.items():
459	        nonterm = ("n/a" if m.non_termination_rate is None
460	                   else f"{m.non_termination_rate:.3f} "
461	                        f"[{m.non_termination_rate_ci_low:.3f}, "
462	                        f"{m.non_termination_rate_ci_high:.3f}]")
463	        out.append(
464	            f"\n## {name}\n\n"
465	            f"- episodes: {m.n_samples}\n"
466	            f"- success rate: {m.accuracy:.3f} "
467	            f"[{m.accuracy_ci_low:.3f}, {m.accuracy_ci_high:.3f}]\n"
468	            f"- mean completion tokens: {m.mean_token_count:.1f}\n"
469	            f"- mean steps: {m.mean_steps}\n"
470	            f"- underthinking rate: {m.underthinking_rate}\n"
471	            f"- overthinking rate: {m.overthinking_rate}\n"
472	            f"- non-termination rate: {nonterm}\n"
473	            f"- unsupported-claim rate: {m.unsupported_claim_rate}\n"
474	            f"- mean verification depth: {m.mean_verification_depth}\n"
475	            f"- stop reasons: {m.stop_reasons}\n"
476	        )
477	    return "".join(out)

1	class ReasoningGymEnvAdapter:
2	    """TRL environment_factory adapter for the OpenEnv reasoning_gym env.
3	
4	    TRL's GRPOTrainer creates one instance per rollout slot, calls reset(**row)
5	    (whose return becomes the prompt), exposes every *other* public method as a
6	    tool the model may call, and reads the task reward off `self.reward`. The
7	    public surface is therefore deliberately exactly {reset, answer}: any extra
8	    public method would be registered as a tool and shown to the model.
9	
10	    The adapter wraps a *synchronous* OpenEnv client (EnvClient.sync()). The
11	    client and action class are injectable so the unit tests exercise the
12	    adapter logic without the OpenEnv install or a running server. reasoning_gym
13	    is single-step: one answer ends the episode.
14	    """
15	
16	    def __init__(self, base_url, env_config=None, client=None, action_cls=None):
17	        self._env_config = dict(env_config or {})
18	        self._client = client if client is not None else self._connect(base_url)
19	        self._action_cls = action_cls
20	        self.reward = 0.0
21	        # Termination flag, same contract as the multi-turn adapters. Single-step:
22	        # the episode terminates iff the model actually called `answer`. Without
23	        # it, "never answered" and "answered wrong" are both reward 0.0 and the
24	        # non-termination reward cannot tell them apart.
25	        self.done = False
26	
27	    @staticmethod
28	    def _connect(base_url):
29	        # Lazy: the reasoning_gym client lives in the cloned OpenEnv repo's
30	        # envs/ package (not on PyPI), and EnvClient is async by default - the
31	        # .sync() wrapper is required because TRL rejects async tools.
32	        from reasoning_gym_env import ReasoningGymEnv
33	
34	        return ReasoningGymEnv(base_url).sync()
35	
36	    def _action(self, answer):
37	        if self._action_cls is None:
38	            from reasoning_gym_env import ReasoningGymAction
39	
40	            self._action_cls = ReasoningGymAction
41	        return self._action_cls(answer=answer)
42	
43	    def reset(self, *, seed=None, prompt=None, **_row):
44	        """Reset to a fresh reasoning_gym question; return the question text.
45	
46	        TRL appends the returned string to the prompt's last user message, then
47	        applies the tool-calling chat template. `prompt` and any other dataset
48	        columns arrive here as kwargs and are ignored - only `seed` selects the
49	        question (deterministic), with dataset name/config from env_config. size
50	        is pinned to 1: one question per episode for this single-step env.
51	        """
52	        reset_kwargs = {"size": 1}
53	        name = self._env_config.get("dataset_name") or self._env_config.get("dataset")
54	        if name is not None:
55	            reset_kwargs["dataset_name"] = name
56	        dataset_config = self._env_config.get("dataset_config")
57	        if dataset_config is not None:
58	            reset_kwargs["dataset_config"] = dataset_config
59	        if seed is not None:
60	            reset_kwargs["seed"] = seed
61	        result = self._client.reset(**reset_kwargs)
62	        self.reward = 0.0
63	        self.done = False
64	        return result.observation.question
65	
66	    def answer(self, answer: str) -> str:
67	        """Submit your final answer to the current problem.
68	
69	        TRL renders this method into the tool spec the model sees, so the
70	        summary above and the Args description below are the tool's
71	        model-facing documentation. transformers' get_json_schema requires a
72	        Google-style Args entry for every parameter.
73	
74	        Args:
75	            answer: The final answer to submit for the current question.
76	        """
77	        result = self._client.step(self._action(answer))
78	        self.reward = float(result.observation.score)
79	        self.done = True
80	        return f"Recorded answer: {answer}"
81

7	class CosineLengthReward:
8	    """Correctness-coupled cosine length reward (Wu/Yeo 2025, "Demystifying
9	    Long CoT"; Kimi-style length scaling).
10	
11	    For a completion of `n_tokens`, let progress = min(n_tokens / max_len, 1)
12	    and c = cos(progress * pi) - so c = +1 for an empty completion and c = -1
13	    at the length cap. The reward interpolates between a short-end and a
14	    long-end value, with the endpoints chosen by correctness:
15	
16	        correct: short -> r_correct_short, long -> r_correct_long   (short > long)
17	        wrong:   short -> r_wrong_short,   long -> r_wrong_long     (short < long)
18	
19	    Correct answers are rewarded more when shorter (concise reasoning); wrong
20	    answers are penalized less when longer (don't punish the model for thinking
21	    before failing). Wrong-and-short is therefore the most-penalized cell.
22	
23	    Under the default `advantage_weighted` composer every component is z-scored
24	    per prompt-group, which cancels any global positive scalar. A purely monotone
25	    signal (e.g. a plain length penalty) z-scores to pure rank order - "shorter
26	    always ranks higher" - so the model drives length to the format-envelope
27	    floor. This reward is non-linear in length *and* gated by correctness, so it
28	    survives z-scoring with real structure: a wrong 17-token completion lands in
29	    the worst cell instead of the best one.
30	
31	    Tradeoff: the length signal now carries correctness information, partially
32	    overlapping the `env_reward` component. That is acceptable under independent
33	    per-component z-scoring and is the intended Wu/Yeo coupling.
34	
35	    Agentic-only: correctness is read from the live OpenEnv instances TRL passes
36	    as kwargs['environments'] (env.reward >= CORRECT_REWARD_THRESHOLD; graded
37	    scorers hand partial credit to near-misses, so a bare > 0 gates wrong).
38	    There is no answer column.
39	    """
40	
41	    def __init__(
42	        self,
43	        tokenizer,
44	        max_len: int,
45	        r_correct_short: float = 1.0,
46	        r_correct_long: float = 0.5,
47	        r_wrong_short: float = -1.0,
48	        r_wrong_long: float = -0.5,
49	    ) -> None:
50	        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
51	        self.max_len = max(int(max_len), 1)
52	        self.r_correct_short = r_correct_short
53	        self.r_correct_long = r_correct_long
54	        self.r_wrong_short = r_wrong_short
55	        self.r_wrong_long = r_wrong_long
56	
57	    def _reward(self, n_tokens: int, correct: bool) -> float:
58	        progress = min(n_tokens / self.max_len, 1.0)
59	        c = math.cos(progress * math.pi)  # +1 at length 0, -1 at max_len
60	        if correct:
61	            lo, hi = self.r_correct_long, self.r_correct_short
62	        else:
63	            lo, hi = self.r_wrong_long, self.r_wrong_short
64	        return lo + 0.5 * (hi - lo) * (1.0 + c)
65	
66	    def __call__(self, prompts, completions, **kwargs) -> list[float]:
67	        # Agentic (environment_factory): TRL passes the live env instances as
68	        # kwargs['environments']; correctness is env.reward > 0 (no answer column).
69	        environments = kwargs.get("environments")
70	        if environments is None:
71	            raise ValueError(
72	                "CosineLengthReward requires kwargs['environments'] (agentic mode). "
73	                "TRL's environment_factory path supplies the live env instances."
74	            )
75	        correct_flags = [
76	            float(getattr(e, "reward", 0.0)) >= CORRECT_REWARD_THRESHOLD
77	            for e in environments
78	        ]
79	        # Prefer the exact model-generated token ids TRL/the rollout_func provide
80	        # over re-encoding decoded text, so the length signal counts model tokens
81	        # only. Falls back to re-encoding the decoded completion.
82	        provided_ids = kwargs.get("completion_ids")
83	        scores = []
84	        for i, completion in enumerate(completions):
85	            ids_i = provided_ids[i] if (provided_ids is not None and i < len(provided_ids)) else None
86	            n_tokens = self._n_tokens(completion, ids_i)
87	            scores.append(self._reward(n_tokens, correct_flags[i]))
88	        return scores
89	
90	    @staticmethod
91	    def _is_multiturn(completion) -> bool:
92	        # Multi-turn iff TRL interleaved a tool-result (game feedback) message.
93	        # In that case completion_ids over-counts (it includes tool tokens), so
94	        # fall back to the assistant-only re-encode.
95	        return isinstance(completion, list) and any(
96	            isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("role") == "tool" for m in completion
97	        )
98	
99	    def _n_tokens(self, completion, completion_ids_i) -> int:
100	        # Single-turn: prefer the exact model-generated ids TRL provides (no
101	        # re-encode) - keeps reasoning_gym numbers identical. Multi-turn: count
102	        # assistant tokens only, excluding injected feedback.
103	        if not self._is_multiturn(completion) and completion_ids_i is not None:
104	            return len(completion_ids_i)
105	        return model_token_count(completion, self.tokenizer)
106

17	def model_token_count(completion, tokenizer) -> int:
18	    """Count the model's own (assistant) tokens in a completion.
19	
20	    TRL hands reward functions the full multi-turn stream, with the game/tool
21	    feedback it injects between turns interleaved as `role == "tool"` messages.
22	    The efficiency reward must measure the model's output, not that feedback, so:
23	
24	    - a string completion (single-turn plain text) is encoded whole;
25	    - a message-list completion sums only `role == "assistant"` content, plus the
26	      serialized arguments of any tool calls the model emitted, and skips tool
27	      messages;
28	    - a lone message dict encodes its content.
29	
30	    `reasoning_content` is summed alongside `content` and that is not optional.
31	    transformers' chat parser splits a Qwen3 response so that the think block
32	    lands in `reasoning_content` on any assistant message carrying a tool call,
33	    leaving `content` empty; only the final tool-less message keeps its `<think>`
34	    inline. Counting `content` alone measured 18 tokens of a 1024-token
35	    completion in e28 - about 2% - which made the cosine length reward a near
36	    constant. See RUNNING.md.
37	
38	    Re-encoding assistant content is a documented approximation of the exact
39	    generated-token count (chat-template framing differs slightly); it counts the
40	    model's actual content tokens, which is the quantity of interest.
41	    """
42	    def _enc(text) -> int:
43	        if not text:
44	            return 0
45	        return len(tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False))
46	
47	    if isinstance(completion, str):
48	        return _enc(completion)
49	
50	    if isinstance(completion, dict):
51	        return _enc(completion.get("content") or "") + _enc(completion.get("reasoning_content") or "")
52	
53	    if isinstance(completion, list):
54	        total = 0
55	        for msg in completion:
56	            if not isinstance(msg, dict) or msg.get("role") != "assistant":
57	                continue
58	            total += _enc(msg.get("content") or "")
59	            total += _enc(msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
60	            for call in (msg.get("tool_calls") or []):
61	                fn = (call or {}).get("function") or {}
62	                args = fn.get("arguments")
63	                if args is None:
64	                    continue
65	                total += _enc(args if isinstance(args, str) else json.dumps(args))
66	        return total
67	
68	    return 0

92	def _bootstrap_ci(values: np.ndarray, n_bootstrap: int = N_BOOTSTRAP, ci: float = 0.95) -> tuple[float, float]:
93	    """Bootstrap CI for the mean of continuous `values` (e.g. token counts).
94	    Vectorized: one (n_bootstrap, n) index draw instead of a Python loop, so
95	    10k replicates cost about what 2k used to. Deterministic via fixed RNG seed.
96	
97	    For a binary proportion (accuracy, thinking rates) prefer `_wilson_ci`:
98	    a percentile bootstrap on a 0/1 vector collapses to a zero-width [p, p]
99	    interval at p=0 or p=1, hiding all uncertainty.
100	    """
101	    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
102	    n = len(values)
103	    if n == 0:
104	        return 0.0, 0.0
105	    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
106	    idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=(n_bootstrap, n))
107	    boot = values[idx].mean(axis=1)
108	    alpha = (1 - ci) / 2
109	    return float(np.percentile(boot, 100 * alpha)), float(np.percentile(boot, 100 * (1 - alpha)))

112	def _wilson_ci(n_success: int, n: int, ci: float = 0.95) -> tuple[float, float]:
113	    """Wilson score interval for a binomial proportion. Unlike a
114	    percentile-bootstrap on the 0/1 vector, it stays a proper interval at the
115	    boundaries: 6/6 -> ~[0.61, 1.0] rather than the degenerate [1.0, 1.0].
116	    Clamped to [0, 1]; returns (0, 0) for n=0.
117	    """
118	    if n == 0:
119	        return 0.0, 0.0
120	    z = float(norm.ppf(1 - (1 - ci) / 2))
121	    phat = n_success / n
122	    denom = 1 + z * z / n
123	    center = (phat + z * z / (2 * n)) / denom
124	    half = (z / denom) * np.sqrt(phat * (1 - phat) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n))
125	    return max(0.0, center - half), min(1.0, center + half)

128	def _thinking_rate(
129	    all_tokens: np.ndarray,
130	    corrects: np.ndarray,
131	    percentile: int,
132	    override: float | None,
133	    side: str,
134	    n_bootstrap: int = N_BOOTSTRAP,
135	    ci: float = 0.95,
136	) -> tuple[float | None, float | None, float | None, float | None]:
137	    """Over/under-thinking rate with a CI that reflects threshold uncertainty.
138	
139	    `side` is 'under' (token <= threshold) or 'over' (token > threshold). The
140	    rate is the fraction of CORRECT completions on the matching side. The
141	    threshold is the `percentile` of ALL token counts (correct + incorrect),
142	    unless `override` is set.
143	
144	    Returns (rate, threshold, ci_low, ci_high), or all-None when there are no
145	    correct samples.
146	
147	    Two CI regimes:
148	      - override set -> threshold is fixed, so the rate is a clean proportion;
149	        use Wilson (no boundary collapse at rate 0/1).
150	      - percentile -> the threshold is itself estimated, so recompute it inside
151	        every bootstrap replicate; its variance then enters the CI (T2.3).
152	    """
153	    all_tokens = np.asarray(all_tokens, dtype=float)
154	    corrects = np.asarray(corrects, dtype=bool)
155	    n = len(all_tokens)
156	    n_correct = int(corrects.sum())
157	    if n_correct == 0:
158	        return None, None, None, None
159	
160	    thr = float(override) if override is not None else float(np.percentile(all_tokens, percentile))
161	    flagged = (all_tokens <= thr) if side == "under" else (all_tokens > thr)
162	    rate = float(flagged[corrects].mean())
163	
164	    if override is not None:
165	        k = int(flagged[corrects].sum())
166	        lo, hi = _wilson_ci(k, n_correct, ci)
167	        return rate, thr, lo, hi
168	
169	    # Percentile threshold: resample all samples, recompute the threshold per
170	    # replicate, then the rate over the resampled correct subset.
171	    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
172	    idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=(n_bootstrap, n))
173	    bt = all_tokens[idx]                                   # (B, n)
174	    bc = corrects[idx]                                     # (B, n)
175	    thr_b = np.percentile(bt, percentile, axis=1, keepdims=True)  # (B, 1)
176	    flag_b = (bt <= thr_b) if side == "under" else (bt > thr_b)
177	    num = (flag_b & bc).sum(axis=1)
178	    den = bc.sum(axis=1)
179	    valid = den > 0
180	    if not valid.any():
181	        return rate, thr, rate, rate
182	    rates = num[valid] / den[valid]
183	    alpha = (1 - ci) / 2
184	    return rate, thr, float(np.percentile(rates, 100 * alpha)), float(np.percentile(rates, 100 * (1 - alpha)))

187	def _offtarget_panel(results: list[SampleResult]) -> dict:
188	    """Off-target behavior metrics (RQ2) from episode termination records.
189	
190	    Returns {} when no result carries `terminated` (dataset-mode results, or
191	    reports produced before trajectory recording existed), so the panel is
192	    absent rather than falsely zero.
193	
194	    Rates use Wilson intervals, not a bootstrap: these are binary proportions
195	    and a percentile bootstrap collapses to a zero-width interval at 0 or 1 -
196	    which is exactly where a non-termination rate sits on a healthy policy.
197	    """
198	    known = [r for r in results if r.terminated is not None]
199	    if not known:
200	        return {}
201	
202	    n = len(known)
203	    n_nonterm = sum(1 for r in known if not r.terminated)
204	    lo, hi = _wilson_ci(n_nonterm, n)
205	    panel = {
206	        "non_termination_rate": n_nonterm / n,
207	        "non_termination_rate_ci_low": lo,
208	        "non_termination_rate_ci_high": hi,
209	        "stop_reasons": dict(sorted(Counter(
210	            r.stop_reason for r in known if r.stop_reason is not None
211	        ).items())),
212	    }
213	
214	    # Verification depth is only defined for episodes that actually finished:
215	    # an episode that ran out of turns never had the chance to claim completion.
216	    finished = [r for r in known if r.terminated and r.tool_calls is not None]
217	    if finished:
218	        depths = [max(len(r.tool_calls) - 1, 0) for r in finished]
219	        n_bare = sum(1 for d in depths if d == 0)
220	        lo_b, hi_b = _wilson_ci(n_bare, len(finished))
221	        panel.update(
222	            unsupported_claim_rate=n_bare / len(finished),
223	            unsupported_claim_rate_ci_low=lo_b,
224	            unsupported_claim_rate_ci_high=hi_b,
225	            mean_verification_depth=float(np.mean(depths)),
226	        )
227	    return panel

230	def compute_metrics(
231	    results: list[SampleResult],
232	    underthinking_percentile: int = 10,
233	    overthinking_percentile: int = 75,
234	    n_bootstrap: int = N_BOOTSTRAP,
235	    underthinking_threshold: float | None = None,
236	    overthinking_threshold: float | None = None,
237	) -> EvalMetrics:
238	    """
239	    Compute all thesis metrics from per-sample results.
240	
241	    underthinking_rate: fraction of CORRECT completions whose token count is
242	    at or below the per-split percentile (default P10) of ALL completions.
243	    Flags correct answers produced with unusually little reasoning relative
244	    to the split — likely lucky pattern-matching rather than genuine
245	    derivation. The threshold adapts to dataset verbosity so the metric
246	    behaves consistently across GSM-8K (short) and MATH (long).
247	
248	    overthinking_rate: fraction of CORRECT completions whose token count exceeds
249	    the per-split percentile (default P75) of ALL completions' token counts.
250	    Captures wasted reasoning — the inverse failure mode to underthinking.
251	    Both thresholds are computed over all samples (correct + incorrect) so the
252	    threshold reflects the population's overall verbosity, not just the
253	    correct-subset distribution. Requires at least 4 samples for the
254	    percentile to be meaningful.
255	
256	    pearson_difficulty_length: Pearson r between difficulty score and mean token count.
257	    Positive r means the model spends more tokens on harder problems - desired behaviour.
258	    Requires difficulty labels (MATH levels 1-5); returns None for GSM-8K / DAPO.
259	
260	    accuracy_ci_low/high: 95% bootstrap confidence interval for accuracy.
261	    """
262	    if not results:
263	        return EvalMetrics()
264	
265	    n = len(results)
266	    n_correct = sum(r.correct for r in results)
267	    accuracy = n_correct / n
268	
269	    all_tokens = np.array([r.n_tokens for r in results], dtype=float)
270	    mean_tokens = float(all_tokens.mean())
271	    tokens_ci_low, tokens_ci_high = _bootstrap_ci(all_tokens, n_bootstrap=n_bootstrap)
272	
273	    steps = [r.n_steps for r in results if r.n_steps is not None]
274	    mean_steps = float(np.mean(steps)) if steps else None
275	
276	    correct_results = [r for r in results if r.correct]
277	
278	    # Absolute-threshold overrides (e.g. from a fixed reference run via
279	    # load_reference_thresholds) take precedence over the per-run percentile.
280	    # When set, they make the over/under-thinking rate comparable across runs;
281	    # when None we fall back to the per-run percentile (back-compatible). An
282	    # override also bypasses the n>=4 percentile-stability guard, since the
283	    # threshold no longer depends on this run's sample size.
284	    under_override = underthinking_threshold
285	    over_override = overthinking_threshold
286	
287	    # Both under- and overthinking use a per-split percentile of all token
288	    # counts as the threshold (unless overridden), then count correct samples
289	    # on the matching side. Thresholds are computed once on the observed sample
290	    # and held fixed during the bootstrap — the reported CI is on the rate
291	    # conditional on the observed threshold.
292	    corrects_mask = np.array([r.correct for r in results], dtype=bool)
293	
294	    # Over/under-thinking rates. The threshold (per-split percentile of all token
295	    # counts, or a fixed reference override) is itself estimated, so T2.3
296	    # recomputes it inside each bootstrap replicate to fold its variance into the
297	    # CI — unless an absolute override fixes it, where a Wilson interval on the
298	    # clean proportion is exact. The n>=4 guard keeps the percentile stable; an
299	    # override bypasses it (the threshold no longer depends on this sample size).
300	    underthinking_rate = underthinking_threshold = None
301	    under_ci_low = under_ci_high = None
302	    if correct_results and (n >= 4 or under_override is not None):
303	        underthinking_rate, underthinking_threshold, under_ci_low, under_ci_high = _thinking_rate(
304	            all_tokens, corrects_mask, underthinking_percentile, under_override, "under",
305	            n_bootstrap=n_bootstrap,
306	        )
307	
308	    overthinking_rate = overthinking_threshold = None
309	    over_ci_low = over_ci_high = None
310	    if correct_results and (n >= 4 or over_override is not None):
311	        overthinking_rate, overthinking_threshold, over_ci_low, over_ci_high = _thinking_rate(
312	            all_tokens, corrects_mask, overthinking_percentile, over_override, "over",
313	            n_bootstrap=n_bootstrap,
314	        )
315	
316	    # Accuracy CI: Wilson, not a percentile bootstrap on the binary vector (which
317	    # collapses to [1, 1] at acc=1.0 — the capability_floor 6/6 case).
318	    ci_low, ci_high = _wilson_ci(n_correct, n)
319	
320	    pearson_val = None
321	    pearson_p = None
322	    with_difficulty = [(r.difficulty, r.n_tokens) for r in results if r.difficulty is not None]
323	    if len(with_difficulty) >= 10:
324	        difficulties = [d for d, _ in with_difficulty]
325	        lengths = [l for _, l in with_difficulty]
326	        # pearsonr returns NaN with a warning when either input is constant.
327	        # Skip the call entirely so the report stays free of NaNs.
328	        if len(set(difficulties)) > 1 and len(set(lengths)) > 1:
329	            r_val, p_val = pearsonr(difficulties, lengths)
330	            pearson_val = float(r_val)
331	            pearson_p = float(p_val)
332	
333	    return EvalMetrics(
334	        accuracy=accuracy,
335	        accuracy_ci_low=ci_low,
336	        accuracy_ci_high=ci_high,
337	        mean_token_count=mean_tokens,
338	        mean_token_count_ci_low=tokens_ci_low,
339	        mean_token_count_ci_high=tokens_ci_high,
340	        underthinking_rate=underthinking_rate,
341	        underthinking_rate_ci_low=under_ci_low,
342	        underthinking_rate_ci_high=under_ci_high,
343	        underthinking_threshold=underthinking_threshold,
344	        overthinking_rate=overthinking_rate,
345	        overthinking_rate_ci_low=over_ci_low,
346	        overthinking_rate_ci_high=over_ci_high,
347	        overthinking_threshold=overthinking_threshold,
348	        pearson_difficulty_length=pearson_val,
349	        pearson_p_value=pearson_p,
350	        mean_steps=mean_steps,
351	        n_samples=n,
352	        n_correct=n_correct,
353	        raw=results,
354	        **_offtarget_panel(results),
355	    )

358	def load_reference_thresholds(
359	    report_path: str,
360	    under_pct: int = 10,
361	    over_pct: int = 75,
362	    min_samples: int = 4,
363	) -> dict[str, dict]:
364	    """Derive fixed over/under-thinking thresholds from a reference eval report.
365	
366	    Reads `report_path` (a run's eval_report.json) and, for each split that
367	    carries a `samples` series, returns the P`under_pct`/P`over_pct` of its token
368	    counts. Thresholds are kept PER SPLIT on purpose: GSM-8K (id_split) and MATH
369	    (near_ood) have legitimately different verbosity, so a single global
370	    threshold would mislabel one of them. Feed the e0 accuracy-only baseline here
371	    so every run's thinking rates are measured against the same yardstick.
372	
373	    Returns `{split: {"underthinking_threshold": float, "overthinking_threshold": float}}`,
374	    skipping splits with fewer than `min_samples` samples.
375	    """
376	    with open(report_path) as f:
377	        report = json.load(f)
378	    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
379	    for split, metrics in (report.get("results") or {}).items():
380	        samples = (metrics or {}).get("samples")
381	        if not samples or len(samples) < min_samples:
382	            continue
383	        tokens = np.array([s["n_tokens"] for s in samples], dtype=float)
384	        out[split] = {
385	            "underthinking_threshold": float(np.percentile(tokens, under_pct)),
386	            "overthinking_threshold": float(np.percentile(tokens, over_pct)),
387	        }
388	    return out

7	class TokenEntropyReward:
8	    """
9	    Mean per-token Shannon entropy H_t = -sum p log p over the policy's
10	    next-token distribution at each *completion* position, conditioned on
11	    the prompt that produced the rollout.
12	
13	    Implementation:
14	    - Renders each prompt through the tokenizer's chat template (with
15	      add_generation_prompt=True).
16	    - Concatenates prompt + completion ids per row, pads to a common length,
17	      and forwards through the current policy in inference mode.
18	    - Picks the logits at positions [p_len-1 .. p_len+c_len-2] for each row
19	      (logits[t] predict token t+1), so entropy reflects the uncertainty
20	      over the actually emitted completion tokens *given the prompt*, not
21	      the unconditional distribution over re-tokenized completion text.
22	
23	    Approximation note: the forward pass uses the *current* (post-update)
24	    policy rather than the policy that produced the rollout. Subword
25	    boundaries from re-decoding may also differ slightly from
26	    generation-time tokenization. Both effects are small in practice but
27	    the reward should be read as a proxy.
28	
29	    fork_mask_top_frac: if >0, average only over tokens in the top fraction
30	    by entropy (inspired by Wang 2025, high-entropy "forking" tokens). Focuses
31	    reward on actual decision points. Expressed as a fraction in [0, 1] — e.g.
32	    0.25 for "top 25%". Values >1 are rejected to prevent the prior pct/frac
33	    ambiguity that produced silent torch.quantile crashes.
34	
35	    NOTE: this masks the *reward* — it restricts which completion tokens enter
36	    the entropy mean — not the *gradient*. Wang 2025 masks the policy gradient
37	    so only high-entropy forking tokens are updated; that is a different
38	    mechanism operating inside the GRPO loss, not a reward function. Read any
39	    fork-mask result as "reward computed over top-entropy tokens", not as
40	    Wang-style gradient masking.
41	    """
42	
43	    def __init__(
44	        self,
45	        model,
46	        tokenizer,
47	        reward_scale: float = 0.1,
48	        fork_mask_top_frac: float = 0.0,
49	        max_seq_length: int | None = None,
50	        chunk_size: int = 4,
51	    ) -> None:
52	        if not 0.0 <= fork_mask_top_frac <= 1.0:
53	            raise ValueError(
54	                f"fork_mask_top_frac must be in [0, 1] (got {fork_mask_top_frac}). "
55	                "Pass a fraction like 0.25, not a percent like 25."
56	            )
57	        if chunk_size < 1:
58	            raise ValueError(f"chunk_size must be >= 1 (got {chunk_size})")
59	        self.model = model
60	        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
61	        self.reward_scale = reward_scale
62	        self.fork_mask_top_frac = fork_mask_top_frac
63	        # Cap concatenated prompt+completion length to keep the forward pass
64	        # within the model's context window. Defaults to the tokenizer's max
65	        # if available; falls back to 4096.
66	        self.max_seq_length = max_seq_length or getattr(tokenizer, "model_max_length", 4096) or 4096
67	        # Rows per forward pass. Materialising (B, T, V) fp32 entropy
68	        # tensors blows up VRAM (Qwen-7B V≈152k → ~2.4 GB per intermediate
69	        # at B=8, T=500). Builder picks the default: 1 when vLLM is
70	        # co-resident (tight headroom), 4 otherwise. Direct instantiation
71	        # defaults to 4 — drop to 1 if you hit OOM.
72	        self.chunk_size = chunk_size
73	
74	    def _prompt_to_text(self, prompt) -> str:
75	        if isinstance(prompt, str):
76	            return prompt
77	        return self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
78	            prompt, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False
79	        )
80	
81	    def __call__(self, prompts, completions, **kwargs) -> list[float]:
82	        if not completions:
83	            return []
84	
85	        prompt_texts = [self._prompt_to_text(p) for p in prompts]
86	
87	        prompt_ids = [
88	            self.tokenizer(pt, add_special_tokens=False).input_ids
89	            for pt in prompt_texts
90	        ]
91	        # Prefer TRL-provided completion_ids (exact ids the policy produced)
92	        # over re-tokenising the decoded text. Re-tokenisation drifts for
93	        # byte-fallback tokens and silently biases entropy on those rows.
94	        provided_ids = kwargs.get("completion_ids")
95	        if provided_ids is not None and len(provided_ids) == len(completions):
96	            comp_ids = [list(c) for c in provided_ids]
97	        else:
98	            comp_texts = [extract_content(c) for c in completions]
99	            comp_ids = [
100	                self.tokenizer(ct, add_special_tokens=False).input_ids
101	                for ct in comp_texts
102	            ]
103	
104	        full_ids: list[list[int]] = []
105	        prompt_lens: list[int] = []
106	        comp_lens: list[int] = []
107	        for p, c in zip(prompt_ids, comp_ids):
108	            seq = (p + c)[: self.max_seq_length]
109	            p_len = min(len(p), len(seq))
110	            c_len = max(len(seq) - p_len, 0)
111	            full_ids.append(seq)
112	            prompt_lens.append(p_len)
113	            comp_lens.append(c_len)
114	
115	        # Bail out cleanly if no completion tokens survived truncation.
116	        if all(c < 1 for c in comp_lens) or all(len(s) < 2 for s in full_ids):
117	            return [0.0] * len(completions)
118	
119	        pad_id = self.tokenizer.pad_token_id
120	        if pad_id is None:
121	            pad_id = self.tokenizer.eos_token_id
122	
123	        device = self.model.device
124	        n = len(completions)
125	        scores: list[float] = [0.0] * n
126	
127	        # Chunked forward + entropy. Keeps peak VRAM bounded by chunk_size
128	        # rather than full batch. Per-chunk we slice [start:end] *before*
129	        # promoting to fp32, so the giant (B, T, V) fp32 intermediates the
130	        # old vectorised path produced never exist.
131	        for chunk_start in range(0, n, self.chunk_size):
132	            chunk_end = min(chunk_start + self.chunk_size, n)
133	            chunk_ids = full_ids[chunk_start:chunk_end]
134	            chunk_max = max(len(s) for s in chunk_ids)
135	
136	            input_ids = torch.tensor(
137	                [s + [pad_id] * (chunk_max - len(s)) for s in chunk_ids],
138	                dtype=torch.long, device=device,
139	            )
140	            attention_mask = torch.tensor(
141	                [[1] * len(s) + [0] * (chunk_max - len(s)) for s in chunk_ids],
142	                dtype=torch.long, device=device,
143	            )
144	
145	            with torch.inference_mode():
146	                logits = self.model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask).logits
147	
148	            for j, abs_i in enumerate(range(chunk_start, chunk_end)):
149	                p_len = prompt_lens[abs_i]
150	                c_len = comp_lens[abs_i]
151	                if p_len < 1 or c_len < 1:
152	                    continue
153	                # logits[t] predict token t+1; completion tokens occupy
154	                # positions [p_len .. p_len+c_len-1], so we want entropy at
155	                # [p_len-1 .. p_len+c_len-2].
156	                start = p_len - 1
157	                end = p_len + c_len - 1
158	                # Slice first → only (c_len, V) reaches fp32, not (T, V).
159	                sl = logits[j, start:end].float()
160	                if sl.numel() == 0:
161	                    continue
162	                log_probs = F.log_softmax(sl, dim=-1)
163	                h_i = -(log_probs.exp() * log_probs).sum(dim=-1)
164	                del sl, log_probs
165	                if self.fork_mask_top_frac > 0.0:
166	                    threshold = torch.quantile(h_i, 1.0 - self.fork_mask_top_frac)
167	                    h_i = h_i[h_i >= threshold]
168	                if h_i.numel() > 0:
169	                    scores[abs_i] = self.reward_scale * h_i.mean().item()
170	
171	            del logits, input_ids, attention_mask
172	
173	        return scores
174

21	class _ComponentMetricsCallback(TrainerCallback):
22	    """Drain the composer's per-component reward metrics into the trainer log.
23	
24	    TRL only sees one composed reward function, so it logs a single
25	    rewards/<composer>/{mean,std}; the individual env/length/entropy
26	    contributions are invisible. transformers.Trainer.log() appends the log
27	    entry to state.log_history BEFORE calling on_log, so updating `logs` alone
28	    is too late — the persisted entry is already a copy. We update that
29	    just-appended entry in place (state.log_history[-1]) so the metrics land in
30	    train_log.json next to reward/kl/loss, and also update `logs` for any live
31	    logger (wandb/trackio). Purely observational: it never touches the composed
32	    reward or the advantage math.
33	    """
34	
35	    def __init__(self, composer) -> None:
36	        self.composer = composer
37	
38	    def on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kwargs):
39	        if not hasattr(self.composer, "pop_step_metrics"):
40	            return
41	        metrics = self.composer.pop_step_metrics()
42	        if not metrics:
43	            return
44	        # state.log_history[-1] is this step's entry (appended just before this
45	        # hook fires); update it in place so the metrics persist to train_log.
46	        if logs is not None:
47	            logs.update(metrics)
48	        if state is not None and getattr(state, "log_history", None):
49	            state.log_history[-1].update(metrics)

57	def build_reward_components(config: dict, domain, runner: GRPORunner) -> list:

62	    method = rewards_cfg.get("compose_method", "advantage_weighted")
63	    for w in warn_inert_scalars(rewards_cfg, method):
64	        print(f"⚠  {w}")

66	    components = []

69	        cfg = rewards_cfg.get(key) or {}

78	def apply_smoke_overrides(config: dict) -> dict:
79	    """Patch config for fast smoke testing: 3 steps, 2 rollouts, short seq.
80	
81	    Sets `_smoke=True` so downstream eval also caps to 10 samples per split.
82	    """
83	    config.setdefault("model", {})
84	    config.setdefault("training", {})
85	    # Pick a smoke context that clears the env's prompt but fits the L4. A 512 cap
86	    # rejected finqa's ~700-token tool-rich prompt outright; the full 4096 OOMs the
87	    # policy-grad backward under vLLM colocate. 2048 holds the prompt plus a few
88	    # turns and leaves room for the step. (Don't go below the config when it is
89	    # already smaller, e.g. a 1024-context model.)
90	    seq = min(int(config["model"].get("max_seq_length", 2048) or 2048), 2048)
91	    config["model"]["max_seq_length"] = seq
92	    # Under colocate the backward competes with vLLM's KV pool for the 24 GB, so
93	    # give training headroom in smoke (0.6 util OOMs a full agentic rollout here).
94	    # Set before --vllm's setdefault so this wins.
95	    config["model"]["gpu_memory_utilization"] = min(
96	        float(config["model"].get("gpu_memory_utilization", 0.45) or 0.45), 0.45
97	    )
98	    # Safety: the completion budget is max_seq - max_prompt_length, so keep the
99	    # prompt cap at half the context (a config with max_prompt_length == max_seq
100	    # would otherwise leave zero room to generate).
101	    config["training"]["max_prompt_length"] = min(
102	        int(config["training"].get("max_prompt_length", seq // 2) or seq // 2), seq // 2
103	    )
104	    config["training"]["max_steps"] = 3
105	    config["training"]["save_steps"] = 3
106	    config["training"]["n_rollouts"] = 2
107	    config["training"]["dataset_size_limit"] = 64
108	    # Cap eval generation: a multi-turn agentic eval runs many model.generate
109	    # calls per episode, and the default budget (max_seq - max_prompt) lets each
110	    # produce ~1k tokens, so a smoke eval can take 20+ minutes. 256 is plenty to
111	    # emit a tool call for a sanity check.
112	    config.setdefault("eval", {})
113	    config["eval"]["max_new_tokens"] = 256
114	    config["_smoke"] = True
115	    print(f"⚠  Smoke mode: max_steps=3, n_rollouts=2, max_seq_length={seq} (<=2048), "
116	          f"gpu_memory_utilization={config['model']['gpu_memory_utilization']}, "
117	          f"max_prompt_length={config['training']['max_prompt_length']}, dataset_size_limit=64, eval=10/split")
118	    return config

72	    """Freeze a per-seed variant of `base_cfg` and return its path.
73	
74	    Subprocess CLIs (training.train / eval.runner) only accept --config, so a
75	    seed / experiment_id override has to travel through a real config file

89	def _expand_configs(patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
90	    """Expand a mix of explicit paths and globs; dedupe; preserve sorted order."""
91	    seen: set[str] = set()
92	    out: list[str] = []
93	    for p in patterns:
94	        matches = sorted(glob.glob(p)) if any(c in p for c in "*?[") else [p]
95	        if not matches:
96	            print(f"Warning: no matches for {p!r}")
97	            continue
98	        for m in matches:
99	            ap = os.path.abspath(m)
100	            if ap in seen:
101	                continue
102	            if not os.path.isfile(ap):
103	                print(f"Warning: not a file: {m!r}")
104	                continue
105	            seen.add(ap)
106	            out.append(m)
107	    return sorted(out)

109	
110	def _tee_subprocess(cmd: list[str], log_path: str) -> int:
111	    """Run `cmd`, streaming combined stdout/stderr to log file and parent stdout.
112	
113	    Returns the subprocess exit code. The log file is overwritten each call.
114	    """
115	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(log_path), exist_ok=True)
116	    header = f"$ {' '.join(cmd)}\n"
117	    print(header, end="", flush=True)
118	    with open(log_path, "w") as log:
119	        log.write(header)
120	        log.flush()
121	        proc = subprocess.Popen(
122	            cmd,
123	            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
124	            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
125	            text=True,
126	            bufsize=1,
127	        )
128	        assert proc.stdout is not None
129	        for line in proc.stdout:
130	            print(line, end="", flush=True)
131	            log.write(line)
132	            log.flush()
133	        return proc.wait()
134	
135	
136	def _run_phase(cmd: list[str], log_path: str, retries: int) -> tuple[str, int, float]:
137	    """Run `cmd` with retry. Returns (status, attempts, duration_s)."""
138	    attempts = 0
139	    t0 = time.time()
140	    while attempts <= retries:
141	        attempts += 1
142	        rc = _tee_subprocess(cmd, log_path)
143	        if rc == 0:
144	            return STATUS_OK, attempts, time.time() - t0
145	        print(f"⚠  Exit {rc} on attempt {attempts}/{retries + 1}", flush=True)
146	    return STATUS_FAIL, attempts, time.time() - t0

165	def _is_real_report(path: str) -> bool:
166	    """True only for a finished, non-stub, non-smoke eval report. Existence
167	    alone is insufficient: a status:'error'/'skipped' stub or a --smoke report
168	    must not be mistaken for finished overnight work."""
169	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
170	        return False
171	    try:
172	        with open(path) as f:
173	            data = json.load(f)
174	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
175	        return False
176	    return data.get("status") not in ("skipped", "error") and not data.get("smoke", False)

185	def _write_eval_stub(config_path: str, status: str, note: str = "") -> bool:
186	    """Backstop for T0.5: guarantee runs/<exp>/eval_report.json exists even when
187	    the eval phase produced none — eval skipped before the subprocess ran (no
188	    checkpoint / train failed), or a hard crash (OOM-kill) that killed runner.py
189	    before it wrote its own error stub. Never overwrites an existing report
190	    (runner.py's stub, or a real one). Returns True if it wrote a stub.
191	    """
192	    try:
193	        cfg = _load_config(config_path)
194	    except Exception:
195	        return False
196	    exp_id = cfg.get("experiment_id")
197	    if not exp_id:
198	        return False
199	    path = os.path.join(_run_dir(exp_id), "eval_report.json")
200	    if os.path.exists(path):
201	        return False
202	    stub = {
203	        "experiment_id": exp_id,
204	        "model_slug": (cfg.get("model") or {}).get("slug"),
205	        "seed": cfg.get("seed", 42),
206	        "compose_method": (cfg.get("rewards") or {}).get("compose_method", "advantage_weighted"),
207	        "status": status,
208	        "results": {},
209	    }
210	    if note:
211	        stub["note"] = note
212	    os.makedirs(_run_dir(exp_id), exist_ok=True)
213	    with open(path, "w") as f:
214	        json.dump(stub, f, indent=2)
215	    print(f"  Wrote stub eval_report.json (status={status}) for {exp_id}: {note}")
216	    return True

219	def _run_train_phase(
220	    config_path: str,
221	    exp_id: str,
222	    smoke: bool,
223	    force: bool,
224	    retries: int,
225	    vllm: bool = False,
226	) -> PhaseResult:
227	    if not force and _is_real_checkpoint(exp_id):
228	        return PhaseResult(status=STATUS_SKIP, note="checkpoint-final exists")
229	
230	    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "training.train", "--config", config_path]
231	    if smoke:
232	        cmd.append("--smoke")
233	    if force:
234	        cmd.append("--overwrite")
235	    if vllm:
236	        cmd.append("--vllm")
237	
238	    log_path = os.path.join(_run_dir(exp_id), "batch_train.log")
239	    status, attempts, dur = _run_phase(cmd, log_path, retries)
240	    return PhaseResult(status=status, duration_s=dur, attempts=attempts, log_path=log_path)

243	def _run_eval_phase(
244	    config_path: str,
245	    exp_id: str,
246	    smoke: bool,
247	    force: bool,
248	    retries: int,
249	    require_checkpoint: bool,
250	) -> PhaseResult:
251	    if require_checkpoint and not _checkpoint_exists(exp_id):
252	        return PhaseResult(status=STATUS_SKIP, note="no checkpoint to eval")
253	    if not force and _is_real_report(os.path.join(_run_dir(exp_id), "eval_report.json")):
254	        return PhaseResult(status=STATUS_SKIP, note="eval_report.json exists")
255	
256	    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "eval.runner", "--config", config_path]
257	    if smoke:
258	        cmd.append("--smoke")
259	
260	    log_path = os.path.join(_run_dir(exp_id), "batch_eval.log")
261	    status, attempts, dur = _run_phase(cmd, log_path, retries)
262	    return PhaseResult(status=status, duration_s=dur, attempts=attempts, log_path=log_path)

265	def _format_duration(sec: float) -> str:
266	    if sec < 60:
267	        return f"{sec:.0f}s"
268	    m, s = divmod(int(sec), 60)
269	    if m < 60:
270	        return f"{m}m{s:02d}s"
271	    h, m = divmod(m, 60)
272	    return f"{h}h{m:02d}m"

280	    results: list[ExperimentResult],
281	    enabled_phases: list[str],
282	    out_path: str,
283	    total_duration_s: float,
284	) -> None:
285	    lines = [
286	        "# Batch run summary",
287	        "",
288	        f"Generated: {datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')}",
289	        f"Total wall time: {_format_duration(total_duration_s)}",
290	        f"Experiments: {len(results)}",
291	        f"Phases: {', '.join(enabled_phases)}",

293	        "| Experiment | Model | " + " | ".join(p.capitalize() for p in enabled_phases) + " | Notes |",
294	        "|---|---|" + "|".join([":---:"] * len(enabled_phases)) + "|---|",

297	        cells = [r.experiment_id, r.model_slug]
298	        notes = []
299	        for p in enabled_phases:
300	            pr = r.phases.get(p)
301	            if pr is None:
302	                cells.append("—")
303	            else:
304	                cell = _status_icon(pr.status)
305	                if pr.status == STATUS_OK and pr.duration_s > 0:
306	                    cell += f" ({_format_duration(pr.duration_s)}"
307	                    if pr.attempts > 1:
308	                        cell += f", {pr.attempts} attempts"
309	                    cell += ")"
310	                elif pr.status == STATUS_FAIL:
311	                    cell += f" ({pr.attempts} attempts)"
312	                cells.append(cell)
313	                if pr.note:
314	                    notes.append(f"{p}: {pr.note}")
315	        cells.append("; ".join(notes) if notes else "")
316	        lines.append("| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
317	
318	    with open(out_path, "w") as f:

338	def _parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
339	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
340	        description="Batch runner: train and/or eval a list of configs.",
341	        formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter,
342	    )
343	    parser.add_argument(
344	        "configs",
345	        nargs="+",
346	        help="Config paths or shell globs (e.g. configs/e5-*.yaml)",
347	    )
348	    parser.add_argument("--train", action="store_true", help="Train each config")
349	    parser.add_argument("--eval", action="store_true", help="Run eval.runner per config")
350	    parser.add_argument("--seeds", nargs="+", type=int, default=None,
351	                        help="Replicate each config across these training seeds (e.g. --seeds 42 43 44). "
352	                             "Each seed gets its own run dir <experiment_id>-s<seed>. "
353	                             "Omit for a single run at the config's own seed.")
354	    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="Pass --smoke to every subprocess")
355	    parser.add_argument("--vllm", action="store_true", help="Pass --vllm to training subprocesses (route GRPO rollouts through vLLM)")
356	    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
357	                        help="Re-run phases even if their output already exists (train passes --overwrite)")
358	    parser.add_argument("--retries", type=int, default=1,
359	                        help="Retry count per failed phase before giving up")
360	    parser.add_argument("--summary-dir", default="runs",
361	                        help="Directory to write batch_summary_<timestamp>.md")
362	    args = parser.parse_args()
363	
364	    # Default to train+eval when no phase flag is given - the most common
365	    # overnight invocation. Explicit `--eval` alone (or `--train` alone) only
366	    # does that one phase.
367	    if not (args.train or args.eval):
368	        args.train = True
369	        args.eval = True
370	
371	    if args.retries < 0:
372	        parser.error("--retries must be ≥ 0")
373	    return args
