# e27bs4 / e28bs4 / e29bs4: the browsergym E1/E2/E3 arms

Harvested 2026-08-10. MiniWoB via browsergym (`click-menu-2`, `click-dialog-2`),
Qwen3-1.7B + LoRA, seed 42, 150 GRPO steps at `batch_size: 4`, `n_rollouts: 8`,
`compose_method: naive_sum`, 100 held-out + 100 shifted eval episodes per arm.

| arm | condition | reward config |
|---|---|---|
| e27bs4 | E1 | `env_reward` only (the lambda=0 control) |
| e28bs4 | E2 | `env_reward` + `token_length` (cosine, w 1.0, max_len 4096) |
| e29bs4 | E3 | `env_reward` + `non_termination` (w 1.0, i.e. lambda=1) |

Diffing the frozen `runs/*/config.yaml` files outside the `description` block leaves
exactly the added reward key in each case, so the one-knob rule holds mechanically and
not just by intent. All three arms answered the identical 100 held-out seeds
(42100000-42100099) and the identical 100 shifted seeds (42200000-42200099), so every
comparison below is paired.

## Headline (held_out)

| | e27bs4 (E1) | e28bs4 (E2) | e29bs4 (E3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.670 [0.573, 0.754] | 0.650 [0.553, 0.736] | 0.640 [0.542, 0.727] |
| non-termination rate | 0.140 [0.085, 0.221] | 0.220 [0.150, 0.311] | 0.090 [0.048, 0.162] |
| correct-episode mean tokens | 930.8 | 776.3 | 845.4 |
| correct-episode median tokens | 680.0 | 435.0 | 630.0 |
| stop: env_done | 86 | 78 | 91 |
| stop: hit_generation_cap | 5 | 18 | 0 |
| stop: no_tool_call | 9 | 3 | 9 |
| stop: max_turns | 0 | 1 | 0 |

Accuracy is flat: every Wilson interval overlaps every other, and no pairwise McNemar
comes close (E1-E2 p = 0.83, E1-E3 p = 0.65, E2-E3 p = 1.00). Nothing about task
success is claimed from this campaign.

The arms separate on the last four rows, and they move in opposite directions. That
is the result.

## E2 compresses correct episodes, and the compression is paired-significant

55 questions both E1 and E2 answered correctly:

| statistic | value | 95% CI (paired bootstrap, 20k) |
|---|---|---|
| difference of medians | -86.0 | [-321.0, +29.0] |
| median of per-question differences | -60.0 | [-160.0, -7.0] |
| mean of per-question differences | -67.9 | [-130.0, -0.6] |
| E2 shorter / longer / tied | 36 / 19 / 0 | sign test p = 0.0300 |

Quartiles over the same 55 questions:

| | Q1 | median | Q3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| e27bs4 | 268.5 | 398.0 | 1379.0 |
| e28bs4 | 243.0 | 312.0 | 1074.0 |
| delta | -25.5 | -86.0 | -305.0 |

Two of the three intervals exclude zero and the sign test clears 0.05, on a
correctness-matched set. The compression again grows with length, which is the shape a
correctness-gated cosine is supposed to produce. The difference-of-medians interval is
wide because the correct-episode distribution is bimodal (the two task families sit at
roughly 250 and 1400 tokens), so which family the bootstrap happens to straddle moves
the median a long way; the per-question differences do not have that problem.

This is the second arm in a row, on a different environment, where the paired
statistics point the same way as e25bs4 did on `polynomial_equations`. It is still one
seed each.

## E2 pays for it in truncation, not in accuracy

Stop-reason transitions, per question, E1 to E2 on held_out:

| E1 | E2 | n |
|---|---|---|
| env_done | env_done | 73 |
| env_done | hit_generation_cap | 12 |
| no_tool_call | hit_generation_cap | 6 |
| hit_generation_cap | env_done | 5 |
| no_tool_call | no_tool_call | 3 |
| env_done | max_turns | 1 |

E2 rescues all 5 of E1's truncations and creates 18 new ones. Paired McNemar on the
`terminated` flag: 13 questions non-terminating only in E2 against 5 only in E1,
p = 0.096.

The mechanism is in the reward definition, not in a bug. The cosine pays
wrong-and-long more than wrong-and-short by construction (`r_wrong_long = -0.5`,
`r_wrong_short = -1.0`), so on any episode the policy is going to fail, the reward
gradient points at generating more. On `polynomial_equations` that incentive had
nowhere to go: every wrong episode already sat at the cap. Here roughly a third of
episodes are wrong and they started with headroom, so the reward spent it. E2 shortens
the episodes it solves and lengthens the ones it does not.

Read as an efficiency result that is a genuine cost, not a wash: mean tokens over
*all* episodes actually rise (1347.9 to 1452.4) while correct-episode tokens fall. This
is exactly the confound `mean_token_count_correct` exists to separate, and here it
separates in the direction that makes the pooled number misleading in E2's favour if
you read it the other way round.

Note that six of the new truncations came from `no_tool_call` episodes. Those are
episodes where E1's policy gave up silently and E2's kept generating. Whether that is
better behaviour is a judgement, not a measurement; it is not more correct.

## E3 removes truncation, not premature stopping

Stop-reason transitions, E1 to E3 on held_out:

| E1 | E3 | n |
|---|---|---|
| env_done | env_done | 86 |
| no_tool_call | no_tool_call | 9 |
| hit_generation_cap | env_done | 5 |

That is the whole table. Every single episode either kept its stop reason or was one of
the 5 truncations that became `env_done`. Paired McNemar on `terminated`: 5 to 0,
p = 0.0625.

The e29bs4 config states the target explicitly: "the target behaviour is premature
stopping rather than truncation wearing a behavioural label". Premature stopping is
`no_tool_call`, and it did not move at all - 9 before, 9 after, and not merely 9 in
aggregate but the same 9 questions. What the penalty removed is the category the config
argued was *not* what it was aimed at.

That is not a null, it is a specific finding about the training signal. During training
the non-termination indicator is `1[env never reported done]`, which covers truncation
and silent stopping identically. The policy found the cheaper of the two: finishing
before the cap is a length adjustment, whereas emitting a tool call on a question you
cannot parse is a capability change. Under a penalty that cannot tell them apart, the
first is what gets optimised.

Two consequences worth carrying into the writeup:

- The E3 non-termination number should not be quoted as evidence about premature
  stopping without this decomposition beside it.
- A version of E3 that penalises `no_tool_call` specifically, leaving truncation to the
  cap, is the experiment that would actually test the RQ2 claim. That is a reward
  change, not a knob.

## RQ2's substitution prediction did not appear in E3

The prediction to test was the reverse of E2's: if premature stopping falls, does
completion length rise, the agent buying termination with tokens?

56 questions both E1 and E3 answered correctly:

| statistic | value | 95% CI (paired bootstrap, 20k) |
|---|---|---|
| difference of medians | -83.5 | [-143.5, +142.0] |
| median of per-question differences | +7.0 | [-57.0, +27.0] |
| mean of per-question differences | +6.4 | [-82.9, +97.1] |
| E3 shorter / longer / tied | 26 / 30 / 0 | sign test p = 0.6889 |

Flat in both directions. No substitution, and no compression either, which is expected
since E3 carries no length term. E3's arm-level `mean_token_count_correct` is *lower*
than E1's (845.4 vs 930.8) purely because E1's five 4096-token truncations are gone
from the pool.

## The gradient is matched for E3 and not for E2

`frac_reward_zero_std` over the 150 training steps (a prompt-group with zero
within-group reward variance produces zero advantage and trains on nothing):

| | e27bs4 | e28bs4 | e29bs4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean `frac_reward_zero_std` | 0.477 | 0.000 | 0.420 |
| live prompt-groups | 52.3% | 100.0% | 58.0% |
| fully-dead steps | 3.3% | 0.0% | 2.0% |
| same, first 30 / last 30 steps | 0.508 / 0.442 | 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.417 / 0.492 |

E2 receives 1.91x the live gradient of its own control, for the same reason as
e25bs4: rollout lengths differ inside a prompt-group even when all eight agree on the
answer, so the cosine gives every group variance (its `frac_reward_zero_std` is exactly
0.0 at every one of the 150 steps). The E1-E2 contrast is therefore "cosine reward plus
roughly twice the live gradient", and the compression result above inherits that
caveat.

E3 is close to matched at 1.11x, because the non-termination indicator is binary and
constant within most groups. The E1-E3 contrast is clean, and the finding it produces -
the penalty targets truncation - is not explainable by a gradient difference.

Other training-side numbers, all three arms over 150 steps:

| | e27bs4 | e28bs4 | e29bs4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EnvReward` raw mean | 0.7081 | 0.7106 | 0.7079 |
| `EnvReward` contrib_l1 | 0.7081 | 0.7106 | 0.7079 |
| `CosineLengthReward` contrib_l1 | - | 0.8455 | - |
| `NonTerminationPenalty` contrib_l1 | - | - | 0.1317 |
| `NonTerminationPenalty` raw mean | - | - | -0.1317 |
| mean completion length | 1464.4 | 1459.4 | 1482.6 |
| terminated-only length | 1424.3 | 1417.5 | 1429.0 |
| same, last 30 steps | 1371.0 | 1333.8 | 1377.2 |
| `clipped_ratio` | 0.0208 | 0.0221 | 0.0292 |
| `tools/call_frequency` | 2.150 | 2.135 | 2.158 |
| kl | 0.00224 | 0.00280 | 0.00232 |
| step time | 350.4 s | 351.0 s | 355.7 s |

Train-time task reward is identical to three decimals across the arms, so no arm
learned the task better than another; whatever the rewards did, they did it to
behaviour and not to competence. The cosine's contribution is comparable in magnitude
to the env reward (1.19x) rather than dominating it as it did at w=16 in the poly
campaign (39x). The non-termination penalty is a fifth of the env reward's magnitude:
13.2% of training rollouts were non-terminating, so lambda=1 buys it a small voice by
construction.

Train-time lengths barely differ, including in the last 30 steps (E2 is 2.7% below E1).
The eval-time compression is much larger than the train-time one, which is worth a
second look at some point - eval is greedy and training samples, so they are not the
same distribution, but the gap is bigger than that alone comfortably explains.

## The shifted split shows nothing

| | e27bs4 | e28bs4 | e29bs4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.800 [0.711, 0.867] | 0.820 [0.733, 0.883] | 0.790 [0.700, 0.858] |
| non-termination rate | 0.200 | 0.170 | 0.200 |
| correct-episode mean tokens | 478.3 | 510.5 | 472.6 |

Every paired statistic on `shifted` is null, in all three pairings and in both
directions: median of per-question differences +3.5 (E1-E2), +0.0 (E1-E3), sign tests
p = 0.64 and p = 1.00. Stop-reason transitions are near-diagonal for both treatments.

The straightforward reading is that there is nothing to compress. Correct episodes on
`navigate-tree` / `click-checkboxes-transfer` run 470-510 tokens against 780-930 on the
held-out families, and 20% of episodes are `no_tool_call` in every arm - the shifted
families fail by not acting, which no length reward addresses. So E2's compression does
not transfer out of distribution, but this split cannot distinguish "does not transfer"
from "has no room to transfer into".

## Unlike the poly campaign, accuracy here is a real measurement

On the e24bs4/e25bs4 pair, every wrong episode sat at the cap and
`non_termination_rate` equalled `1 - accuracy` exactly, so accuracy measured whether the
model finished inside the budget. That is not the case here. Wrong episodes on held_out
split as:

| | env_done (wrong but finished) | hit_generation_cap | no_tool_call |
|---|---|---|---|
| e27bs4 | 19 | 5 | 9 |
| e28bs4 | 13 | 18 | 3 (+1 max_turns) |
| e29bs4 | 27 | 0 | 9 |

Most failures are episodes that acted, terminated, and got it wrong. Correct episodes
are 100% `env_done` in all three arms. So on browsergym, accuracy and termination are
genuinely separate quantities and the E3 condition has something of its own to measure -
which was the qualification bar the config set for this task mix.

E3's wrong-and-terminated count rising from 19 to 27 is the other side of the truncation
removal: the penalty converts unfinished episodes into finished wrong ones, and three of
those five conversions came back correct.

## Residual limits

- **One seed per arm.** The poly w-sweep produced a seed pair whose medians swapped
  under replication. Seeds 43/44 are the minimum before E2's compression is claimed as
  a direction rather than an observation.
- **E2 is not gradient-matched** (1.91x live groups). E3 is.
- **Under/overthinking rates in the three reports are not comparable.** Each derives
  its thresholds from its own token distribution. Use `load_reference_thresholds`
  against a fixed reference before quoting them.
- **No E0 comparison yet.** The base-model arm on disk predates the current seed scheme,
  so none of these numbers has an untrained reference point. The re-eval is queued.
- **The unsupported-claim and verification-depth panel is weak here.** Two tools, and
  `click` is both the acting and the terminal call, so "terminal tool called with
  nothing before it" fires on any one-step success. Read the numbers in the reports as
  a step-count proxy, not as verification behaviour.

## Provenance

Wall time 52h39m: e27bs4 train 14h56m + eval 2h30m, e28bs4 14h57m + 2h43m, e29bs4
15h09m + 2h22m. Batch summary `batch_summary_20260810_000818.md`. Run directories are in
this folder minus checkpoints; the paired statistics read `episodes_held_out.jsonl` and
`episodes_shifted.jsonl` from each, bootstrap RNG seeded at 0.

    finished = [r for r in known if r.terminated and r.tool_calls is not None]

29	    )

32	def base_model_conflict(run_dir: str) -> str | None:
33	    """Error message if E0 results would overwrite a trained run, else None.
34	
35	    run_dir keys on experiment_id alone, so `--base-model` against a trained
36	    arm's config used to overwrite its eval_report.json and episodes_*.jsonl

38	    config and its own experiment_id (the e0 / e0b pattern).
39	    """

41	        return None
42	    return (
43	        f"--base-model would write E0 results into {run_dir!r}, which holds a "
44	        "trained checkpoint. Use a dedicated E0 config with its own "
45	        "experiment_id (see configs/e0-*.yaml)."
46	    )
47	
48

51	    import sys
52	
53	    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__)))
54

62	    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="Limit eval to 4 episodes per split")
63	    args = parser.parse_args()
64	
65	    with open(args.config) as f:
66	        config = yaml.safe_load(f)
67	
68	    # Same guard training gets. An eval-only invocation used to skip validation
69	    # entirely, so a typo'd key here was caught only if the config had also been
70	    # through `training.train` at some point.
71	    from training.config_schema import validate_config
72	    validate_config(config)
73	
74	    exp_id = config["experiment_id"]
75	    run_dir = os.path.join("runs", exp_id)
76	
77	    if args.smoke:
78	        conflict = smoke_conflict(run_dir)
79	        if conflict:
80	            parser.error(conflict)
81	        config["_smoke"] = True
82	        print("Smoke mode: eval limited to 4 episodes per split")
83

## Analysis: `pipeline/runs/e27bs4_e28bs4_e29bs4_findings.md`

Accuracy null everywhere. Pairwise McNemar: E1-E2 p=0.83, E1-E3 p=0.65, E2-E3 p=1.00.

**E2 compression is real at one seed.** 55 both-correct held-out questions:

| statistic | value | CI (paired bootstrap 20k) |
|---|---|---|
| median of per-question diffs | -60.0 | [-160.0, -7.0] |
| mean of per-question diffs | -67.9 | [-130.0, -0.6] |
| shorter/longer/tied | 36/19/0 | sign test p = 0.030 |

Cost: truncation 5 -> 18. Cosine pays wrong-and-long over wrong-and-short by construction. Poly had no headroom (wrong episodes already at cap); browsergym did, so the reward spent it. Pooled mean tokens actually rise (1347.9 -> 1452.4) while correct-episode tokens fall.

**E3's stop-reason table has one off-diagonal cell in 100 questions:** 5 `hit_generation_cap` -> `env_done`. `no_tool_call` stayed at 9, and at the same 9 questions. The training indicator is `1[env never reported done]`, which cannot separate truncation from silent stopping, so the policy took the cheap one. The config named premature stopping as the target; premature stopping did not move.

**Gradient:** E2 `frac_reward_zero_std` = exactly 0.0 at all 150 steps vs control 0.477, so 1.91x live groups - the compression carries that confound. E3 at 58.0% vs 52.3% is matched, so its finding is clean.

Shifted split null in all three pairings. Correct episodes there are 470-510 tokens vs 780-930 held-out, so it cannot separate "does not transfer" from "no room".

"""Paired E0-vs-arm comparison on the browsergym bs4 campaign.

Separate from analyze_e27_e29.py on purpose: adding e0 to that script's arm dict
would change its bootstrap draw order and move numbers already written into the
findings file. Bootstrap RNG seeded at 0 here too.
"""
import json
import os

import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import binomtest

RUNS = "/Users/mheidebrecht/Documents/Projects/Uni/Master_Thesis/master-thesis-code/pipeline/runs"
BASE = ("e0", "e0-browsergym-base-qwen3-1_7b")
ARMS = [
    ("e27bs4", "e27bs4-browsergym-e1-baseline-qwen3-1_7b"),
    ("e28bs4", "e28bs4-browsergym-e2-cosine-qwen3-1_7b"),
    ("e29bs4", "e29bs4-browsergym-e3-nontermination-qwen3-1_7b"),
]
SPLITS = ["held_out", "shifted"]
B = 20000


def load(d, split):
    path = os.path.join(RUNS, d, f"episodes_{split}.jsonl")
    with open(path) as f:
        return {r["seed"]: r for r in (json.loads(x) for x in f if x.strip())}


def boot_ci(fn, a, b, rng):
    n = len(a)
    idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=(B, n))
    return tuple(np.percentile([fn(a[i], b[i]) for i in idx], [2.5, 97.5]))


rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

for split in SPLITS:
    print(f"\n{'=' * 70}\nSPLIT: {split}\n{'=' * 70}")
    e0 = load(BASE[1], split)
    common = sorted(e0)

    for name, d in ARMS:
        ex = load(d, split)
        assert sorted(ex) == common, f"{name} answered a different question set"
        print(f"\n--- e0 vs {name} ({split}) ---")

        x_only = [s for s in common if e0[s]["correct"] and not ex[s]["correct"]]
        y_only = [s for s in common if not e0[s]["correct"] and ex[s]["correct"]]
        nd = len(x_only) + len(y_only)
        p = binomtest(len(y_only), nd, 0.5).pvalue if nd else 1.0
        print(f"McNemar: e0-only correct {len(x_only)}, {name}-only correct "
              f"{len(y_only)}, exact two-sided p = {p:.4f}")

        both = [s for s in common if e0[s]["correct"] and ex[s]["correct"]]
        ta = np.array([e0[s]["n_tokens"] for s in both], float)
        tb = np.array([ex[s]["n_tokens"] for s in both], float)
        d_ = tb - ta
        print(f"both correct: n = {len(both)}")
        print(f"  e0 median {np.median(ta):.1f} mean {ta.mean():.1f} | "
              f"{name} median {np.median(tb):.1f} mean {tb.mean():.1f}")
        for lbl, fn in [
            ("difference of medians", lambda x, y: np.median(y) - np.median(x)),
            ("median of per-q diffs", lambda x, y: np.median(y - x)),
            ("mean of per-q diffs", lambda x, y: np.mean(y - x)),
        ]:
            lo, hi = boot_ci(fn, ta, tb, rng)
            print(f"  {lbl}: {fn(ta, tb):+.1f}  CI [{lo:+.1f}, {hi:+.1f}]")
        sh, lg = int((d_ < 0).sum()), int((d_ > 0).sum())
        sp = binomtest(sh, sh + lg, 0.5).pvalue if sh + lg else 1.0
        print(f"  {name} shorter/longer/tied: {sh}/{lg}/{int((d_ == 0).sum())}  "
              f"sign test p = {sp:.4f}")
        q = [25, 50, 75]
        print(f"  quartiles e0: {np.percentile(ta, q).round(1)}  "
              f"{name}: {np.percentile(tb, q).round(1)}")

        a_nt = [s for s in common if not e0[s]["terminated"] and ex[s]["terminated"]]
        b_nt = [s for s in common if e0[s]["terminated"] and not ex[s]["terminated"]]
        ndn = len(a_nt) + len(b_nt)
        pn = binomtest(len(b_nt), ndn, 0.5).pvalue if ndn else 1.0
        print(f"  non-term McNemar: e0-only non-term {len(a_nt)}, "
              f"{name}-only non-term {len(b_nt)}, p = {pn:.4f}")

        trans = {}
        for s in common:
            k = (e0[s]["stop_reason"], ex[s]["stop_reason"])

Two of the three intervals exclude zero and the sign test clears 0.05, on a
correctness-matched set. The compression again grows with length, which is the shape a
correctness-gated cosine is supposed to produce. The difference-of-medians interval is
wide because the correct-episode distribution is bimodal (the two task families sit at
roughly 250 and 1400 tokens), so which family the bootstrap happens to straddle moves
the median a long way; the per-question differences do not have that problem.

The arms separate on the last four rows, and they move in opposite directions. That
is the result.

## E0: training bought no accuracy on this task

`e0-browsergym-base-qwen3-1_7b` re-ran on 2026-08-10 against the identical seeds
(42100000-42100099 and 42200000-42200099, `--base-model`, no adapter, same 4096-token
whole-trajectory budget), so it pairs question for question with all three arms. The
2026-08-03 e0 run does not - it scored the pre-fix seed bases 100042.. and 200042.. -
and is archived on the box rather than quoted here.

| held_out | e0 | e27bs4 (E1) | e28bs4 (E2) | e29bs4 (E3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.680 [0.583, 0.763] | 0.670 | 0.650 | 0.640 |
| non-termination rate | 0.150 | 0.140 | 0.220 | 0.090 |
| correct-episode mean tokens | 1035.6 | 930.8 | 776.3 | 845.4 |

Paired McNemar against e0 on held_out: E1 8 vs 7 discordant (p = 1.00), E2 15 vs 12
(p = 0.70), E3 14 vs 10 (p = 0.54). Not one trained arm beats the untrained model, and
E0's point estimate is nominally the highest of the four. On `shifted` the same holds
(E0 0.810 against 0.800 / 0.820 / 0.790, every McNemar p >= 0.62).

So 150 GRPO steps of env-reward training did not make this policy better at MiniWoB.
Everything below is a comparison between behaviours at equal task competence. That is
still the right question for RQ1/RQ2 - the reward conditions are about *how* the agent
spends tokens and turns, not about whether it wins more - but no sentence in the thesis
should imply the E1 recipe taught the model the task.

The discordant counts are large relative to the differences (15 and 12 flips between
E0 and E2 for a net of -3), so per-question outcomes are noisy while the aggregate is
stable. That is the signature of a policy whose competence did not move and whose
tie-breaking did.

## Training did change length, and it changed it most on the hard family

The pooled accuracy above hides two family-level moves in opposite directions.
`held_out` alternates by seed parity (`tasks[seed % len(tasks)]`), 50 episodes each.

| click-menu-2 (n=50) | e0 | e27bs4 | e28bs4 | e29bs4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.58 | 0.48 | 0.42 | 0.44 |
| correct-episode median tokens | 1963.0 | 1876.0 | 1622.0 | 1463.0 |
| stop: env_done / cap / no_tool | 47/3/12* | 36/5/9 | 28/18/3 | 41/0/9 |

| click-dialog-2 (n=50) | e0 | e27bs4 | e28bs4 | e29bs4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.78 | 0.86 | 0.88 | 0.84 |
| correct-episode median tokens | 275.0 | 301.0 | 271.0 | 261.5 |
| stop: env_done | 50 | 50 | 50 | 50 |

(*e0's held_out stop reasons pooled are 85/3/12; the split above is approximate for e0
only, exact for the three arms.)

Two things fall out.

**`click-dialog-2` is fully solved-and-terminating in every trained arm** - 50 of 50
`env_done`, no truncation, no silent stopping. So the entire non-termination and
truncation story of this campaign is a `click-menu-2` story, and any RQ2 statement
should say so rather than quoting a pooled rate over a set that is half degenerate.

**Training trades the hard family for the easy one.** Accuracy falls 0.58 to 0.42-0.48
on `click-menu-2` and rises 0.78 to 0.84-0.88 on `click-dialog-2`. Pooled, those cancel
to the flat number in the headline. Whether that is the reward or 150 steps of GRPO
sharpening whatever was already easier is not separable here, but it is a real
behavioural change hiding inside a null.

The strongest single length effect in the campaign is E1 against E0 on `click-menu-2`:
on the 24 questions both answered correctly, median difference **-286 tokens**, 23
shorter against 1 longer, sign test p < 0.0001. The env reward alone compresses the
long family hard. E2 and E3 against E0 on the same family are -341 (n=16, p = 0.077)
and -172 (n=17, p = 0.14) - the same direction, smaller n, no added effect that this
seed can resolve.

This **reverses** the corresponding claim in `e27_e1_baseline_findings.md`, which
reported the E1 recipe *inflating* `click-menu-2` length by +247 tokens against E0.
That comparison was between two batch_size 1 runs on the pre-fix seed scheme; under the
bs4 geometry and the current seeds the sign flips. The old number should not be carried
forward.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **`CosineLengthReward` (Wu/Yeo 2025)**: `progress = min(n_tokens/max_len, 1)`, `c = cos(progress*pi)`. Correct: short=1.0, long=0.5. Wrong: short=-1.0, long=-0.5. **Wrong-and-long pays more than wrong-and-short by construction** - this is the mechanism behind E2's truncation increase.
   - **`frac_reward_zero_std`**: TRL metric, fraction of prompt-groups with zero within-group reward variance. Such a group yields zero advantage and trains on nothing. A component that adds within-group variance buys its arm more live gradient than the control gets.
   - **`hit_generation_cap` semantics**: fires when `budget <= 0` at loop start OR when a turn's `n_tok >= turn_cap`. Tool feedback charges the trajectory budget but is NOT added to `n_tokens`, so a cap episode can record n_tokens < 4096 (observed: 3266, 3375, 3521).
   - **Family assignment by seed parity**: `tasks[seed % len(tasks)]` in `domains/browsergym/adapter.py:reset()`. Even seed -> first task, odd -> second. This is what made the per-family decomposition possible.
   - **Seed blocks**: question seed = `config_seed * SEED_BLOCK + offset`, `SEED_BLOCK = 1_000_000`. Eval offset `_EVAL_SEED_OFFSET = 100_000`. New scheme gives 42100000..; the pre-fix scheme gave `seed + offset` = 100042.. - the discriminator for whether a run is paired with the bs4 campaign.
   - **`unsupported_claim_rate`** = fraction of terminated episodes with `len(tool_calls) == 1` (i.e. `max(len-1,0) == 0`), computed in `eval/metrics.py:~226`. Degenerate on browsergym (only `click` and `noop`, no distinguished terminal call).

59	        self._env_config = dict(env_config or {})
60	        # An ABSENT `tasks` takes the default mix; an explicitly EMPTY one is a
61	        # config error. Collapsing the two would silently train the default mix
62	        # under a config that says otherwise.
63	        tasks = self._env_config.get("tasks")
64	        tasks = _DEFAULT_TASKS if tasks is None else tasks

66	        if not self._tasks:

72	    @staticmethod
73	    def _connect(base_url):
74	        # Lazy: the browsergym client lives in the cloned OpenEnv repo's envs/
75	        # package (not on PyPI). .sync() wraps it for TRL, which rejects async
76	        # tools, matching the reasoning_gym pattern.
77	        from browsergym_env import BrowserGymEnv

79	        return BrowserGymEnv(base_url).sync()

81	    def _make_action(self, tool, arguments):
82	        """Tool call -> the browsergym action object.
83	
84	        The one seam that touches the OpenEnv clone on the action path, imported
85	        lazily and kept in a single method so the unit tests can replace it and
86	        run without browsergym installed.
87	        """
88	        from browsergym_env import BrowserGymAction
89	        from browsergym_env.harness import build_browsergym_action_str
90	
91	        return BrowserGymAction(action_str=build_browsergym_action_str(tool, arguments))

93	    def _act(self, tool, **arguments) -> str:
94	        """Send one action and return the resulting page, or the env's error."""
95	        if self.done:
96	            # Done-guard: once the episode is over, further tool calls must not
97	            # overwrite the terminal reward.
98	            return "The episode is already finished; no further actions are accepted."
99	        result = self._client.step(self._make_action(tool, arguments))
100	        # MiniWoB pays out on the terminating step and 0 before it, so last-wins
101	        # is the terminal reward. The done-guard above stops a later call from
102	        # overwriting it.
103	        self.reward = float(getattr(result, "reward", 0.0) or 0.0)
104	        self.done = bool(getattr(result, "done", False))
105	        observation = getattr(result, "observation", None)
106	        error = str(getattr(observation, "error", "") or "")
107	        page = _obs_text(observation)

112	    def reset(self, *, seed=None, prompt=None, **_row):
113	        """Load this seed's page and return its goal plus accessibility tree.
114	
115	        TRL appends the returned string to the prompt's last user message, then
116	        applies the tool-calling chat template. The task family is a pure function
117	        of the seed (`tasks[seed % len(tasks)]`) because the eval loop resets with
118	        a seed and nothing else, and because every rollout slot in a GRPO group
119	        must land on the same page. `prompt` and other dataset columns arrive as
120	        kwargs and are ignored.

122	        s = 0 if seed is None else int(seed)
123	        task = self._tasks[s % len(self._tasks)]
124	        result = self._client.reset(seed=s, task_name=task)
125	        self.reward = 0.0
126	        self.done = False
127	        observation = getattr(result, "observation", None)
128	        goal = str(getattr(observation, "goal", "") or "").strip()
129	        return f"Task: {goal}\n\nPage:\n{_obs_text(observation)}"

24	    """MiniWoB web tasks served through OpenEnv's browsergym env.
25	
26	    Selected over finqa by the feasibility probe

28	    decided it, neither of which finqa had:
29	
30	    1. Difficulty is selectable. MiniWoB spans saturated (click-test 1.00) to
31	       unreachable (click-tab-2 0.00) for Qwen3-1.7B, so a task set can be chosen
32	       inside the 40-80% band where GRPO gets within-group variance and the E1
33	       baseline has headroom. finqa was fixed at 1% with no dial.
34	    2. Task performance and the off-target axis can be decoupled. The default set
35	       mixes click-option (0.50 success, headroom) with click-checkboxes (0.35
36	       success against 0.50 termination, so the axes separate). On a set where
37	       every terminated episode is correct, a non-termination penalty would be
38	       indistinguishable from a task reward and RQ2 would have nothing to measure.
39

41	    the efficiency reward counts assistant tokens across all turns, excluding the
42	    page observations the env injects between them. The dominant base-model
43	    failure is `no_tool_call` - stopping without acting - which is premature
44	    stopping measured directly rather than inferred.

60	        # TRL repeats each row num_generations times to form a GRPO group, and
61	        # reset(seed=...) turns the seed into a deterministic (task, page) pair -
62	        # so every rollout in a group sees the same page, and the mixed task set
63	        # is interleaved evenly by `tasks[seed % len(tasks)]`.
64	        from datasets import Dataset
65	
66	        rows = [
67	            {"prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": _LEAD_IN}], "seed": seed_base + i}
68	            for i in range(int(n))

94	        # argv EnvServerProcess passes, so training.env_server.port must stay at
95	        # the server's own default of 8000. A mismatch is loud (nothing answers
96	        # the client), not silent.
97	        cfg = dict(env_config or {})
98	        tasks = cfg.get("tasks") or ["click-option", "click-checkboxes"]

106	        # reset with "core is not defined".

## The finding: TRL's vLLM correction silently discards most of the gradient, by length

Every link checked (TRL 1.6.0 source on box, harvested train logs):

1. vLLM samples the rollout; the trainer recomputes those tokens' logps with its own forward at the same weights. The two implementations disagree by ~0.018 per token (numerics; logged abs mean).
2. TRL 1.6 defaults `vllm_importance_sampling_mode = "sequence_mask"`. Weight per episode = `exp(signed diff summed over ALL assistant tokens)`; ratio above cap 3.0 gets masked to **0.0**. We never set the key, so every arm ran under it.
3. `grpo_trainer.py:2613`: `per_token_loss = per_token_loss * importance_sampling_ratio`. Weight ~0 means that episode teaches nothing.
4. The sum grows with completion length, so **long episodes systematically collapse to ~0 weight or blow past the cap and get zeroed. Short ones survive.** A length-dependent gradient filter, inside a thesis about length.

Measured, mean over each run: e27bs4 **0.283**, e28bs4 0.291, e29bs4 0.282; poly e24bs4 0.486 (shorter completions). Min 0.0000 at nearly every step, max pinned at 2.996 (the cap). Flat from step 1, which rules out weight-sync staleness.

This explains the whole phenotype in one move. Training EnvReward was **flat all 150 steps** (first-10 mean 0.788, last-30 0.737 - it never rose; the old bs1 "0.375 -> 0.72 rise" was single-page-per-step noise). dialog-2 (~300 tok, survives filter) rose 0.78 -> 0.84-0.88; menu-2 (~2000 tok, filtered) fell 0.58 -> 0.42-0.48. No arm beats E0 because the only headroom was on exactly the family whose gradient got thrown away.

Also settled today: adapter loads fine (only 2/100 E0-vs-E1 episodes have identical token counts), train/eval prompts mirror by construction, eval is greedy HF generate so **eval numbers are untouched** - this is a training-side distortion.

## Exhaustive hypothesis list

**A. Code / pipeline**
1. **TIS sequence_mask filter - prime suspect, evidenced above.** Test: 3-step instrumented probe logging per-episode (length, family, ISR weight, reward). Prediction: weight ~0 above ~1000 tok, menu-2 near-excluded.
2. Reward attribution (reward paired with wrong completion in group) - low probability (plausible raw_mean, tool failure rate 0.0), same probe hand-checks 10 episodes.
3. Greedy-eval vs temp-1 training objective mismatch - demoted: sampled reward is flat too, so the optimizer never gained on its own objective.
4. vLLM weight staleness - refuted (bad at step 1, no decay pattern).
5. Eval-side bugs (adapter, budget, template) - refuted today.

**B. Optimization knobs (live even after A1 is fixed)**
1. lr 5e-6 + LoRA r16 + 150 steps = microscopic updates (grad_norm 0.05, KL 0.003). Test after fix: 50-step probe at lr 2e-5, watch reward slope.
2. Entropy 0.165, half of groups zero-variance - weak exploration. Test: rollout temp 1.2.
3. Mixed families: dialog-2 groups near-saturated (dead), menu-2 carries signal but was filtered. After fix, a menu-2-only probe is the clean learnability test.

**C. Env alignment (your step 2)**
1. `_MAX_OBS_CHARS = 2000` truncation may hide menu-2 targets - if the model can't see the answer, success is luck and nothing is learnable. Test: reset 20 menu-2 seeds, measure tree size, check target visibility.
2. Chance floor unknown: random-click agent, 100 episodes. If ~0.5, base "skill" is mostly luck - your "solving by chance" hypothesis, directly tested.
3. Inspect a few full episodes: what does the page look like after click 1.
4. dialog-2 at 0.78-0.88 sits at/above the 40-80 band top (e26 criterion) - half the batch is near-dead weight; candidate swap from the 15 probed families.

**D. Model (your step 3)**
1. 1.7B capacity: eval Qwen3-4B base on the same seeds (fits L4 for eval-only). menu-2 accuracy is the number - if it jumps, model binds; C2+D1 together answer "too dumb / by chance".

**E. Statistical power (cross-cutting)**
n=100 single-seed McNemar detects only ~15pt effects. But the training log (4800 episodes) is the stronger readout and it independently says flat - power is not the whole story here.

## Ordered plan (your ordering, decisive test first)

1. Box probe for A1+A2 (~30 min): confirm the filter empirically, hand-check reward attribution.
2. Fix ISR handling (`token_truncate` mode vs correction off - decide after probe), new config key + schema + unit test, then a 50-step E1-style probe. **Go/no-go = EnvReward slope finally positive.**
3. C1-C3 env checks, minutes each, same box session.
4. Re-pick task set (C4) on the fixed trainer.
5. Only if menu-2 still flat: D1 model-scale probe.
6. Full E1 re-run only after 1-5; E2/E3 on top only once E1 beats E0.

One consequence to sit with: the poly e24bs4/e25bs4 pair trained under the same filter at ISR 0.49, and the filter suppresses exactly the long-completion gradient the cosine reward works through. # Why does no trained arm beat e0 - audit and fix plan

Started 2026-08-11. The browsergym bs4 campaign (e27bs4/e28bs4/e29bs4) produced
no arm that beats the untrained base model on held-out accuracy (e0 0.680 vs
0.670/0.650/0.640), which breaks the premise of the efficiency study: E2/E3
cannot be read as "efficiency at held accuracy" if E1 itself buys nothing.
This plan lists every hypothesis considered, what the initial audit already
established, and the test order: code first, then environment alignment, then
model scale.

## What the 2026-08-10 audit already established

All of this is verified against TRL 1.6.0 source on the box and the harvested
`train_log.json` files, not inferred.

**Prime suspect: TRL's vLLM importance-sampling correction discards most of the
gradient, preferentially by completion length.**

1. vLLM samples the rollouts; the trainer recomputes the sampled tokens'
   logprobs with its own HF forward at the same weights. The two disagree by
   ~0.018 abs per token (numerics; `sampling/sampling_logp_difference/mean`).
2. TRL 1.6 defaults `vllm_importance_sampling_mode = "sequence_mask"` with
   `clip_max = 3.0`. The per-episode weight is `exp(signed per-token diff
   summed over every assistant token of the episode)`; a ratio above 3.0 is
   masked to exactly 0.0. No config in this repo sets the key, so every vLLM
   run trained under it.
3. `grpo_trainer.py:2613` multiplies the per-token loss by that weight, so an
   episode at weight ~0 contributes no gradient.
4. The summed drift grows with completion length, so long episodes land far
   from ratio 1.0 and lose their gradient; short episodes survive. A
   length-dependent gradient filter, inside a study about length.

Measured run means of `sampling/importance_sampling_ratio/mean`: e27bs4 0.283,
e28bs4 0.291, e29bs4 0.282, e24bs4 (poly) 0.486. Min is 0.0000 at nearly every
step; max sits at the 2.996 cap. The ratio is bad from step 1, which rules out
weight-sync staleness (that would start near 1.0 and decay).

The phenotype this explains: training EnvReward flat across all 150 steps
(first-10 mean 0.788, last-30 0.737 - the optimizer never improved its own
objective; the earlier e27 "0.375 -> 0.72 rise" was single-page-per-step noise
at batch_size 1), click-dialog-2 (~300 tokens, survives the filter) up 0.78 ->
0.84-0.88, click-menu-2 (~2000 tokens, filtered) down 0.58 -> 0.42-0.48, and
no arm beating e0 because the only headroom was on the filtered family.

Also settled on 2026-08-10:

- Eval-side bugs refuted. The LoRA adapter loads and changes behaviour (only
  2/100 held-out episodes have identical token counts between e0 and e27bs4);
  eval is greedy HF `generate` with no vLLM involved, so every eval number on
  disk is untouched by the filter.
- Train/eval prompt construction mirrors by design (same `_LEAD_IN`, same
  reset-return appended, same two tools).
- Greedy-vs-sampled objective mismatch demoted: the sampled (temp 1.0)
  training reward is flat too, so the optimizer never gained on the objective
  it actually optimizes.
- Trainer health context: `tools/failure_frequency` 0.0, grad_norm 0.05-0.09,
  KL ~0.003, entropy ~0.165.

## Hypothesis list

### A. Code / pipeline

- A1 **TIS sequence_mask filter** (prime suspect, evidence above). Decisive
  test: instrumented probe over a few real training steps logging per-episode
  completion length, task family, ISR weight, and reward. Prediction: weight
  ~0 above roughly 1000 tokens, click-menu-2 episodes near-excluded.
- A2 **Reward attribution** (reward paired with the wrong completion inside a
  group). Low probability - plausible raw means, zero tool failures - but the
  same probe dumps (seed, env reward, completion head) for a hand-check of ~10
  episodes.
- A3 Greedy-eval vs temp-1.0 objective mismatch. Demoted (see above); after
  the fix, one temp-1.0 eval documents the gap for the record.
- A4 vLLM weight staleness. Refuted (bad at step 1, no decay pattern).
- A5 Eval-side bugs (adapter load, budget, template). Refuted 2026-08-10.

### B. Optimization knobs (live even after A1 is fixed)

- B1 **Learning rate / adapter capacity too small.** lr 5e-6 with LoRA r16
  gives grad_norm ~0.05 and KL ~0.003 after 150 steps - the policy barely
  moves in distribution space. Test: short probe at lr 2e-5 on the fixed
  trainer; watch the EnvReward slope and clip/KL health.
- B2 **Exploration too weak.** Entropy ~0.165 and about half of all
  prompt-groups have zero reward variance, so many groups carry no learning
  signal. Test: rollout temperature 1.2 probe; watch `frac_reward_zero_std`
  and the reward slope.
- B3 **Mixed families dilute the batch.** click-dialog-2 groups are
  near-saturated (mostly dead under group-relative advantages) while
  click-menu-2 carried the live signal that the filter then discarded. Test:
  click-menu-2-only probe as the clean learnability measurement.

### C. Environment alignment

- C1 **Observation truncation.** The adapter caps the accessibility tree at
  `_MAX_OBS_CHARS = 2000` chars. If click-menu-2 trees exceed that, the model
  cannot see the target and success is partly luck - nothing learnable. Test:
  reset ~20 menu-2 seeds, measure tree sizes, check target visibility.
- C2 **Chance floor unknown.** A random-click scripted agent over 100
  episodes gives the floor; if it lands near the 0.58 base accuracy, base
  "skill" is mostly luck (the "solving by chance" hypothesis, tested
  directly).
- C3 **Interaction pattern.** Inspect several full episode transcripts: what
  the page looks like after the first click, whether the goal stays visible.

24	class _ComponentMetricsCallback(TrainerCallback):
25	    """Drain the composer's per-component reward metrics into the trainer log.
26	
27	    TRL only sees one composed reward function, so it logs a single
28	    rewards/<composer>/{mean,std}; the individual env/length/entropy
29	    contributions are invisible. transformers.Trainer.log() appends the log
30	    entry to state.log_history BEFORE calling on_log, so updating `logs` alone
31	    is too late — the persisted entry is already a copy. We update that
32	    just-appended entry in place (state.log_history[-1]) so the metrics land in
33	    train_log.json next to reward/kl/loss, and also update `logs` for any live
34	    logger (wandb/trackio). Purely observational: it never touches the composed
35	    reward or the advantage math.
36	    """
37	
38	    def __init__(self, composer) -> None:
39	        self.composer = composer
40	
41	    def on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kwargs):
42	        if not hasattr(self.composer, "pop_step_metrics"):
43	            return
44	        metrics = self.composer.pop_step_metrics()
45	        if not metrics:
46	            return
47	        # state.log_history[-1] is this step's entry (appended just before this
48	        # hook fires); update it in place so the metrics persist to train_log.
49	        if logs is not None:
50	            logs.update(metrics)
51	        if state is not None and getattr(state, "log_history", None):

"""
Reward registry. Maps a config key (under `rewards:`) to a default weight and
a builder. `train.build_reward_components` iterates this registry instead of
hard-coding branches; new signals only require a builder + entry here plus the
matching key in `config_schema._KNOWN_REWARD_KEYS`.

Each builder has the signature:
    build(domain, runner, training_cfg, reward_cfg) -> Callable
where reward_cfg is the dict under `rewards.<key>` from the YAML.

Agentic-only: `env_reward` is the task-success signal; `token_length` (E2) and
`non_termination` (E3) are the efficiency signals. All default off and are
enabled explicitly per config.
"""
from training.rewards.cosine_length import CosineLengthReward
from training.rewards.env_reward import EnvReward
from training.rewards.non_termination import NonTerminationPenalty


def _build_token_length(domain, runner, training_cfg, cfg):
    # Cosine length reward (Wu/Yeo 2025): correct -> prefer shorter, wrong ->
    # prefer longer. Non-linear and correctness-gated (correctness comes from the
    # env), so it survives the advantage_weighted per-group z-scoring.
    return CosineLengthReward(
        runner.tokenizer,
        max_len=int(cfg.get("max_len", 256)),
        r_correct_short=cfg.get("r_correct_short", 1.0),
        r_correct_long=cfg.get("r_correct_long", 0.5),
        r_wrong_short=cfg.get("r_wrong_short", -1.0),
        r_wrong_long=cfg.get("r_wrong_long", -0.5),
    )


def _build_env_reward(domain, runner, training_cfg, cfg):
    # Task-success reward from the OpenEnv environment. TRL's environment_factory
    # path passes the live env instances as kwargs['environments']; EnvReward
    # reads env.reward off each.
    return EnvReward()


def _build_non_termination(domain, runner, training_cfg, cfg):
    # E3: -1 per episode that never reached the terminal tool. Reads env.done off
    # the same live env instances. No knobs - lambda is the component `weight`.
    return NonTerminationPenalty()

# configs enable env_reward + the efficiency signals explicitly.

    "env_reward":       (False, 1.0, _build_env_reward),
    "non_termination":  (False, 1.0, _build_non_termination),
}

"""TIS filter probe: 3 real training steps of the e27bs4 recipe, instrumented.

Dumps one jsonl record per completion: seed, group, assistant-token count, the
per-sequence importance-sampling weight TRL multiplies into the loss, the raw
summed logp drift behind it, the env reward, the advantage, and the completion
head/tail for the reward-attribution hand-check (plan items A1 + A2).

Runs the production path unmodified: training.train.main() with the real
config, monkeypatched only to (a) swap GRPOTrainer for the instrumented
subclass, (b) redirect the run dir to a throwaway experiment_id, (c) capture
EnvReward's per-completion output. Lives in /workspace, not the repo.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/master-thesis-code/pipeline")

DUMP = "/workspace/probe_tis/probe_dump.jsonl"
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(DUMP), exist_ok=True)

import training.grpo_runner as gr  # noqa: E402  (sets PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF)
import training.train as T  # noqa: E402
from training.rewards.env_reward import EnvReward  # noqa: E402

_LAST = {"env_rewards": None}
_orig_call = EnvReward.__call__


def _capturing_call(self, *args, **kwargs):
    rewards = _orig_call(self, *args, **kwargs)
    try:
        _LAST["env_rewards"] = [float(r) for r in rewards]
    except Exception:
        _LAST["env_rewards"] = None
    return rewards


EnvReward.__call__ = _capturing_call


class ProbeTrainer(gr.GRPOTrainer):
    def _generate_and_score_completions(self, inputs):
        seeds = [r.get("seed") for r in inputs] if isinstance(inputs, list) else []
        out = super()._generate_and_score_completions(inputs)
        try:
            self._probe_dump(seeds, out)
        except Exception as e:
            with open(DUMP, "a") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps({"probe_error": repr(e)}) + "\n")
        return out

    def _probe_dump(self, seeds, out):
        cm = out.get("completion_mask")
        if cm is None:
            with open(DUMP, "a") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps({"probe_error": "no completion_mask",
                                    "keys": sorted(map(str, out.keys()))}) + "\n")
            return
        tm = out.get("tool_mask")
        mask = cm if tm is None else cm * tm
        isr = out.get("importance_sampling_ratio")
        old_lp = out.get("old_per_token_logps")
        samp_lp = out.get("sampling_per_token_logps")
        comp_ids = out.get("completion_ids")
        adv = out.get("advantages")
        env_r = _LAST["env_rewards"]
        tok = self.processing_class
        B = int(cm.shape[0])
        ng = int(self.args.num_generations)
        recs = []
        for i in range(B):
            rec = {
                "step": int(self.state.global_step),
                "i": i,
                "group": i // ng,
                "seed": int(seeds[i]) if i < len(seeds) and seeds[i] is not None else None,
                "asst_tokens": int(mask[i].sum()),
                "completion_tokens": int(cm[i].sum()),
                "n_inputs": len(seeds),
                "batch": B,
            }
            if isr is not None:
                rec["isr_shape"] = list(isr.shape)
                rec["isr_weight"] = float(isr[i].reshape(-1)[0])
            if old_lp is not None and samp_lp is not None:
                rec["sum_logp_diff"] = float(((old_lp[i] - samp_lp[i]) * mask[i]).sum())
            if adv is not None:
                rec["advantage"] = float(adv[i].reshape(-1)[0])
            if env_r is not None and i < len(env_r):
                rec["env_reward"] = env_r[i]
            if comp_ids is not None:
                ids = comp_ids[i][cm[i].bool()]
                text = tok.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=False)
                rec["completion_head"] = text[:400]
                rec["completion_tail"] = text[-300:]
            recs.append(rec)
        with open(DUMP, "a") as f:
            for r in recs:
                f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")


gr.GRPOTrainer = ProbeTrainer

_orig_load = T.load_config


def _probe_load(path):
    cfg = _orig_load(path)
    cfg["experiment_id"] = "probe-tis-filter"
    cfg["training"]["max_steps"] = 3
    cfg["training"]["save_steps"] = 500
    return cfg


T.load_config = _probe_load

sys.argv = ["probe_tis", "--config",
            "configs/e27bs4-browsergym-e1-baseline-qwen3-1_7b.yaml", "--overwrite"]
T.main()

"""TIS filter probe: N real training steps of the e27bs4 recipe, instrumented.

Dumps one jsonl record per completion: seed, group, assistant-token count, the
per-sequence importance-sampling weight TRL multiplies into the loss, the raw
summed logp drift behind it, the env reward, the advantage, and (optionally)
the completion head/tail for the reward-attribution hand-check (plan items
A1 + A2 in docs/plans/no-arm-beats-e0-audit.md).

Runs the production path unmodified: training.train.main() with the real
config, monkeypatched only to (a) swap GRPOTrainer for the instrumented
subclass, (b) redirect the run dir to a throwaway experiment_id, (c) capture
EnvReward's per-completion output. Lives in /workspace, not the repo.

Knobs via env vars so the same script runs both the 3-step diagnostic and the
50-step token_truncate verification (the mode override goes through the real
config key, so it exercises validate_config and the grpo_runner mapping):
    PROBE_CONFIG    config path         (default e27bs4 yaml)
    PROBE_STEPS     max_steps           (default 3)
    PROBE_MODE      vllm_importance_sampling_mode; empty = leave config alone
    PROBE_EXP_ID    experiment_id       (default probe-tis-filter)
    PROBE_DUMP      dump jsonl path     (default /workspace/probe_tis/probe_dump.jsonl)
    PROBE_DUMP_TEXT 1|0 completion head/tail in records (default 1)
"""
import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/master-thesis-code/pipeline")

CONFIG = os.environ.get("PROBE_CONFIG",
                        "configs/e27bs4-browsergym-e1-baseline-qwen3-1_7b.yaml")
STEPS = int(os.environ.get("PROBE_STEPS", "3"))
MODE = os.environ.get("PROBE_MODE", "")
EXP_ID = os.environ.get("PROBE_EXP_ID", "probe-tis-filter")
DUMP = os.environ.get("PROBE_DUMP", "/workspace/probe_tis/probe_dump.jsonl")
DUMP_TEXT = os.environ.get("PROBE_DUMP_TEXT", "1") == "1"
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(DUMP), exist_ok=True)

import training.grpo_runner as gr  # noqa: E402  (sets PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF)
import training.train as T  # noqa: E402
from training.rewards.env_reward import EnvReward  # noqa: E402

_LAST = {"env_rewards": None}
_orig_call = EnvReward.__call__


def _capturing_call(self, *args, **kwargs):
    rewards = _orig_call(self, *args, **kwargs)
    try:
        _LAST["env_rewards"] = [float(r) for r in rewards]
    except Exception:
        _LAST["env_rewards"] = None
    return rewards


EnvReward.__call__ = _capturing_call


class ProbeTrainer(gr.GRPOTrainer):
    def _generate_and_score_completions(self, inputs):
        seeds = [r.get("seed") for r in inputs] if isinstance(inputs, list) else []
        out = super()._generate_and_score_completions(inputs)
        try:
            self._probe_dump(seeds, out)
        except Exception as e:
            with open(DUMP, "a") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps({"probe_error": repr(e)}) + "\n")
        return out

    def _probe_dump(self, seeds, out):
        cm = out.get("completion_mask")
        if cm is None:
            with open(DUMP, "a") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps({"probe_error": "no completion_mask",
                                    "keys": sorted(map(str, out.keys()))}) + "\n")
            return
        tm = out.get("tool_mask")
        mask = cm if tm is None else cm * tm
        isr = out.get("importance_sampling_ratio")
        old_lp = out.get("old_per_token_logps")
        samp_lp = out.get("sampling_per_token_logps")
        comp_ids = out.get("completion_ids")
        adv = out.get("advantages")
        env_r = _LAST["env_rewards"]
        tok = self.processing_class
        B = int(cm.shape[0])
        ng = int(self.args.num_generations)
        recs = []
        for i in range(B):
            rec = {
                "step": int(self.state.global_step),
                "i": i,
                "group": i // ng,
                "seed": int(seeds[i]) if i < len(seeds) and seeds[i] is not None else None,
                "asst_tokens": int(mask[i].sum()),
                "completion_tokens": int(cm[i].sum()),
                "n_inputs": len(seeds),
                "batch": B,
            }
            if isr is not None:
                rec["isr_shape"] = list(isr.shape)
                rec["isr_weight"] = float(isr[i].reshape(-1)[0])
            if old_lp is not None and samp_lp is not None:
                rec["sum_logp_diff"] = float(((old_lp[i] - samp_lp[i]) * mask[i]).sum())
            if adv is not None:
                rec["advantage"] = float(adv[i].reshape(-1)[0])
            if env_r is not None and i < len(env_r):
                rec["env_reward"] = env_r[i]
            if DUMP_TEXT and comp_ids is not None:
                ids = comp_ids[i][cm[i].bool()]
                text = tok.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=False)
                rec["completion_head"] = text[:400]
                rec["completion_tail"] = text[-300:]
            recs.append(rec)
        with open(DUMP, "a") as f:
            for r in recs:
                f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")


gr.GRPOTrainer = ProbeTrainer

_orig_load = T.load_config


def _probe_load(path):
    cfg = _orig_load(path)
    cfg["experiment_id"] = EXP_ID
    cfg["training"]["max_steps"] = STEPS
    cfg["training"]["save_steps"] = max(STEPS * 10, 500)
    if MODE:
        cfg["training"]["vllm_importance_sampling_mode"] = MODE
    return cfg


T.load_config = _probe_load

sys.argv = ["probe_tis", "--config", CONFIG, "--overwrite"]
T.main()

MENU_SEEDS = [42100000 + i for i in range(100) if (42100000 + i) % 2 == 0]
DIALOG_SEEDS = [42100000 + i for i in range(100) if (42100000 + i) % 2 == 1]

results = {"max_obs_chars": _MAX_OBS_CHARS, "c1_obs": [], "c2_random": [],
           "c3_transcripts": []}


def _obs(result):
    o = getattr(result, "observation", None)
    ax = str(getattr(o, "axtree_txt", "") or "")
    goal = str(getattr(o, "goal", "") or "")
    return ax, goal


def _bids(text):
    return re.findall(r"\[(\d+)\]", text)


# C1: obs size + target visibility.
for seed in MENU_SEEDS:
    r = client.reset(seed=seed, task_name="click-menu-2")
    ax, goal = _obs(r)
    quoted = re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', goal)
    target = quoted[-1] if quoted else None
    results["c1_obs"].append({
        "seed": seed, "goal": goal, "ax_len": len(ax), "target": target,
        "target_in_full": bool(target and target in ax),
        "target_in_truncated": bool(target and target in ax[:_MAX_OBS_CHARS]),
    })

# C2: random-click floor, acting on the truncated view.
rng = random.Random(0)
for task, seeds in (("click-menu-2", MENU_SEEDS), ("click-dialog-2", DIALOG_SEEDS)):
    for seed in seeds:
        r = client.reset(seed=seed, task_name=task)
        ax, _ = _obs(r)
        view = ax[:_MAX_OBS_CHARS]
        reward, done, turns = 0.0, False, 0
        while not done and turns < 8:
            cand = _bids(view)
            if not cand:
                break
            act = BrowserGymAction(
                action_str=build_browsergym_action_str("click", {"bid": rng.choice(cand)}))
            res = client.step(act)
            reward = float(getattr(res, "reward", 0.0) or 0.0)
            done = bool(getattr(res, "done", False))
            ax, _ = _obs(res)
            view = ax[:_MAX_OBS_CHARS]
            turns += 1
        results["c2_random"].append({"task": task, "seed": seed,
                                     "reward": reward, "done": done, "turns": turns})

# C3: full transcripts for reading, first three menu seeds.
for seed in MENU_SEEDS[:3]:
    r = client.reset(seed=seed, task_name="click-menu-2")
    ax, goal = _obs(r)
    steps = [{"goal": goal, "ax": ax}]
    cand = _bids(ax)
    if cand:
        res = client.step(BrowserGymAction(
            action_str=build_browsergym_action_str("click", {"bid": cand[0]})))
        ax2, _ = _obs(res)
        steps.append({"after_click": cand[0],
                      "reward": float(getattr(res, "reward", 0.0) or 0.0),
                      "done": bool(getattr(res, "done", False)), "ax": ax2})
    results["c3_transcripts"].append({"seed": seed, "steps": steps})

server.stop()
with open(OUT, "w") as f:
    json.dump(results, f, indent=2)

n_tr = sum(1 for r in results["c1_obs"] if r["target_in_truncated"])
n_full = sum(1 for r in results["c1_obs"] if r["target_in_full"])
lens = sorted(r["ax_len"] for r in results["c1_obs"])
menu = [r for r in results["c2_random"] if r["task"] == "click-menu-2"]
dialog = [r for r in results["c2_random"] if r["task"] == "click-dialog-2"]
print(f"C1: n={len(results['c1_obs'])} target_in_full={n_full} "
      f"target_in_truncated={n_tr} ax_len min/med/max="
      f"{lens[0]}/{lens[len(lens) // 2]}/{lens[-1]}")
print(f"C2 menu   random reward>0.5: {sum(1 for r in menu if r['reward'] > 0.5)}"
      f"/{len(menu)}  done: {sum(1 for r in menu if r['done'])}")
print(f"C2 dialog random reward>0.5: {sum(1 for r in dialog if r['reward'] > 0.5)}"
      f"/{len(dialog)}  done: {sum(1 for r in dialog if r['done'])}")
print("WROTE", OUT)

Prediction confirmed on the first live batch, with a sharper twist than predicted:

- ISR is per-sequence `[32,1]`. **21 of 32 completions carry weight < 0.1** - the effective batch is ~6 episodes, not 32.
- The `exp(sum) > 3 -> 0.0` masking is real: records with positive drift sum (+1.42, +2.56, +1.73) show weight exactly 0.0000.
- The drift is systematically negative (25/32), so even short dialog-2 completions get crushed (mean weight ~0.19 in that group). At browsergym lengths everything is deep in the collapse regime.
- **The one live menu-2 group (2 correct / 6 wrong - the only real learning signal in the step) delivers its gradient almost entirely through one lucky correct trajectory at weight 1.29; the other correct one is at 0.005 and the six wrong ones at 0.003-0.64.** The wrong-answer push-down barely exists.
- A2 largely clears: rewards pair correctly (1.00s get advantage +1.62, 0.00s get -0.54, zero-variance groups get exactly 0).

`token_truncate` is the right fix on this evidence: per-token ratios sit at exp(+-0.02) ~ 1, occasional outlier tokens clamp at 3, every episode keeps bounded gradient. Hand-checking A2 completion texts while the remaining two steps run.

**Slope verdict: NO-GO - the fix works mechanically, but fix-alone does not make the reward climb.** B1 (lr probe) is already running per the plan's gate.

The run completed all 50 steps while the VPN was down (results sat on the box; nothing lost). Three findings:

**1. The ISR fix does what it should.** Importance-sampling mean went from 0.28 to 1.0000, the per-token clamp is active (min ratios 0.16-0.18 instead of whole episodes zeroed), and grad_norm doubled to ~0.12. Gradient now flows from every episode, long ones included.

**2. The reward still does not climb.** Per-10-step buckets: 0.766, 0.738, 0.759, 0.606, 0.647. Looks like decline - but it is not. Both runs share seed 42, so they saw the identical prompts at the identical steps, and e27bs4's buckets at the same steps are 0.788, 0.706, 0.728, 0.597, 0.650. Paired per-step difference: **+0.009 mean, 0.000 median, 21 positive / 23 negative.** The two trajectories are statistically indistinguishable; the dip at steps 31-40 is question-difficulty structure, present in both.

**3. Why: the policy barely moves at all.** KL after 50 steps is ~0.002 in both runs. At lr 5e-6 with LoRA r16 and half the groups reward-saturated, 50 steps cannot visibly move the policy no matter how clean the gradient is. The filter was masking a second problem: the optimization is too weak to see.

So the plan's gate fired: Phase 2 moved up. **B1 is live** - same recipe, same seed (so it pairs step-for-step again), `token_truncate`, one knob: `learning_rate: 2e-5` (4x). Pid 769822, started 13:15 UTC, ETA ~18:30 UTC. Frozen config verified to record both the lr and the mode. Watch: reward slope, clip ratio, KL. Monitor armed; RUNNING.md, LAB_NOTES, taskwarrior updated (commit `c69377e`).

Next steps:
1. B1-DONE ~18:30 UTC: paired slope read vs both 5e-6 runs.
2. If B1 climbs: decide task set (C4), then campaign re-run geometry.
3. If B1 flat: B2 (temp 1.2) / B3 (menu-only) probes, then Phase 4 (4B model) as last resort.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **TRL 1.6 vLLM TIS (truncated importance sampling) correction - the found root cause:** vLLM samples rollouts; the trainer recomputes those tokens' logps with its HF forward at the same weights; per-token abs disagreement ~0.018 (numerics). Default `vllm_importance_sampling_mode="sequence_mask"` computes a per-EPISODE weight `exp(SIGNED per-token drift summed over all assistant tokens)`, and `masked_fill(0.0)` outside [min, 3.0]. Applied at `grpo_trainer.py:2613`: `per_token_loss = per_token_loss * inputs["importance_sampling_ratio"]`. The summed drift grows with completion length -> long episodes lose gradient preferentially. `token_truncate` instead clamps per-token ratios (shape [B, T], nearly all ~1.0); `"off"` maps to `vllm_importance_sampling_correction=False`.

ok some stuff i noticed. please evaluate the ideas and see if it effects our work and if we should update our plan @docs/plans/no-arm-beats-e0-audit.md 

The mask is one-sided. Only Δ above the cap is dropped. So you're not just losing long sequences — you're systematically keeping the ones where the training model assigned lower probability than vLLM did. That's a selection effect on top of the length effect, and it biases the surviving gradient in a specific direction rather than just shrinking it.

Temperature scaling. If you sampled at T ≠ 1, check this: vLLM by default returns unprocessed logprobs, so some logprobs are temperature-scaled and some aren't, producing a huge artificial mismatch. The fix is passing logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs" to the vLLM init (vLLM ≥ 0.10.2). If you had this on top of sequence_mask, the 70% figure has a second, cheaper explanation and your "fixed" trainer may not be fully fixed.

And: The zero-slope problem after the fix

This is where I'd push back on your current hypothesis. KL ≈ 0.002 after 50 steps is very small. That's not "policy moving slowly" — that's closer to "policy receiving essentially no gradient." Before spending compute on the LR ladder, rule out these, roughly in order of how cheaply they explain the observation:

1. Group-degenerate advantages. GRPO's advantage is (r − mean(r_group)) / (std(r_group) + ε). If BrowserGym success is near-zero for e0, every group of G rollouts has identical reward, std = 0, advantage = 0 — the gradient is exactly zero, and no learning rate fixes that. Log the fraction of groups with nonzero reward std and mean |Â| per step. If that fraction is low, your bottleneck is task difficulty / reward density, not optimization, and B1 will come back flat at 2e-5 too.

2. beta > 0. If the KL penalty is active (older TRL defaulted to 0.04), it directly pins the policy to the reference. A KL that sits stably at 0.002 across 50 steps is a signature of a KL term winning against a weak reward gradient, not of slow drift. Most modern GRPO recipes run beta=0.0.

3. max_grad_norm. A copy-pasted 0.1 (common in Unsloth-derived configs) will throttle updates hard independent of LR.

4. LoRA LR scale. 5e-6 is a full-finetune learning rate. The rule of thumb from the LoRA-without-regret line of work is that LoRA wants roughly 10× the full-FT LR, so the analog here is ~5e-5. Your B1 at 2e-5 is only 4× — directionally right, possibly still short. Worth planning a 5e-5 rung.

5. LoRA target modules. r16 on q/v only is thin. If you're not hitting the MLP projections, capacity is a real constraint for agentic behavior change.

Also confirm mask_truncated_completions=False — on long agentic rollouts that flag zeroes out entire completions that hit max_completion_length, which is a second length-correlated filter that would reintroduce your original confound under a different name.

16	from training.registry import LORA_TARGET_MODULES, get_model_config
17	
18	
19	class GRPORunner:
20	    """Vanilla TRL + PEFT GRPO. Loads the model (optionally 4-bit nf4), applies
21	    LoRA, and runs GRPOTrainer. The agentic rollout_func branch is added later.
22	    """
23	
24	    def __init__(self, config: dict) -> None:
25	        self.config = config
26	        model_cfg = get_model_config(config["model"]["slug"])
27	
28	        lora_rank = int(config["model"].get("lora_r", model_cfg["max_lora_rank"]))
29	        lora_alpha = int(config["model"].get("lora_alpha", lora_rank * 2))
30	        load_4bit = config["model"].get("load_in_4bit", model_cfg["load_in_4bit"])
31	        max_seq = int(config["model"].get("max_seq_length", model_cfg["max_seq_length"]))
32	        # vLLM colocate is the default generation backend for training. It is
33	        # required for the agentic rollout path and is the only tractable option
34	        # for GRPO on a single GPU. Set model.use_vllm: false to fall back to HF.
35	        use_vllm = config["model"].get("use_vllm", True)
36	
37	        dtype = torch.bfloat16 if torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() else torch.float16
38	
39	        quant_config = None
40	        if load_4bit:
41	            quant_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
42	                load_in_4bit=True,
43	                bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
44	                bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
45	                bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=dtype,
46	            )
47	
48	        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_cfg["model_name"])
49	        self.model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
50	            model_cfg["model_name"],
51	            quantization_config=quant_config,
52	            torch_dtype=dtype,
53	            device_map="auto",
54	        )
55	        self.model.config.use_cache = False
56	
57	        if load_4bit:
58	            self.model = prepare_model_for_kbit_training(
59	                self.model, use_gradient_checkpointing=True
60	            )
61	
62	        lora_config = LoraConfig(
63	            r=lora_rank,
64	            lora_alpha=lora_alpha,
65	            target_modules=LORA_TARGET_MODULES,
66	            lora_dropout=0.0,
67	            bias="none",
68	            task_type="CAUSAL_LM",
69	        )
70	        self.model = get_peft_model(self.model, lora_config)
71	        self.model.enable_input_require_grads()
72	
73	        self._lora_rank = lora_rank
74	        self._max_seq = max_seq
75	        self._use_vllm = use_vllm
76	
77	    def _grpo_config(self, output_dir: str) -> GRPOConfig:
78	        t = self.config["training"]
79	        max_prompt_len = t.get("max_prompt_length", self._max_seq // 2)
80	        max_completion_len = self._max_seq - max_prompt_len
81	
82	        # Bound activation memory: forward/backward completions in small
83	        # micro-batches and accumulate gradients over `batch_size` whole
84	        # prompt-groups per optimizer step.
85	        #
86	        # `batch_size` defaults to 4, not 1, and the difference is not a
87	        # performance knob. TRL centres advantages on the per-group mean
88	        # (grpo_trainer.py:2177, scale_rewards="group"), so a group whose
89	        # rollouts all score alike yields exactly zero advantage. A binary
90	        # env_reward saturates that way ~46% of the time, so at batch_size 1 -
91	        # one group per step - roughly half of all optimizer steps applied a
92	        # zero update. A shaped reward that varies within the group (cosine
93	        # length) does not saturate, so the defect hit env-only baselines about
94	        # twice as hard as the treatment arms they were compared against. A step
95	        # is dead only when every group in it saturates: 0.46^4 = 4.5%.
96	        n_rollouts = int(t.get("n_rollouts", DEFAULT_N_ROLLOUTS))
97	        batch_size = int(t.get("batch_size", DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE))
98	        total_completions = batch_size * n_rollouts
99	        micro = int(t.get("micro_batch_size", 2))
100	        if micro < 1 or total_completions % micro != 0:
101	            micro = 1
102	        grad_accum = total_completions // micro
103	        max_steps = int(t.get("max_steps", 500))
104	        # Print the resolved geometry: cross-arm comparisons are only valid
105	        # between runs that agree on it, and the log is where that is checked.
106	        print(f"Batch geometry: batch_size={batch_size}  n_rollouts={n_rollouts}  "
107	              f"micro_batch_size={micro}  grad_accum={grad_accum}  max_steps={max_steps}")
108	
109	        kwargs = dict(
110	            temperature=float(t.get("temperature", 1.0)),
111	            learning_rate=float(t.get("learning_rate", 5e-6)),
112	            adam_beta1=0.9,
113	            adam_beta2=0.99,
114	            weight_decay=float(t.get("weight_decay", 0.1)),
115	            warmup_ratio=float(t.get("warmup_ratio", 0.1)),
116	            lr_scheduler_type="cosine",
117	            optim="paged_adamw_8bit",
118	            logging_steps=1,
119	            bf16=torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),
120	            fp16=not torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),
121	            gradient_checkpointing=True,
122	            # TRL 1.6 counts per_device_train_batch_size in completions, and a
123	            # full prompt-group is num_generations completions. Micro-batch the
124	            # forward pass and accumulate, so one optimizer step still consumes
125	            # whole groups and max_steps counts steps of `batch_size` prompts.
126	            per_device_train_batch_size=micro,
127	            gradient_accumulation_steps=grad_accum,
128	            num_generations=n_rollouts,
129	            max_completion_length=max_completion_len,
130	            max_steps=max_steps,
131	            save_steps=int(t.get("save_steps", 100)),
132	            output_dir=output_dir,
133	            report_to="none",
134	            beta=float(t.get("kl_beta", 0.001)),
135	            seed=int(self.config.get("seed", 42)),
136	        )
137	        # Cap the tool-calling loop. TRL treats an unset
138	        # max_tool_calling_iterations as sys.maxsize, so leaving it off for
139	        # single-step domains left the loop unbounded: a reasoning_gym rollout
140	        # could call `answer` repeatedly until it filled the completion budget,
141	        # which is itself a mechanism for the cap-bound rollouts the e22/e23 cap
142	        # probes went looking for. resolve_max_turns is shared with the eval
143	        # loop, so an unset env_config.max_turns means the same episode process
144	        # (one iteration) on both sides. max_tool_calling_iterations is a TRL
145	        # 1.6 GRPOConfig field (confirmed at the L4 smoke).
146	        kwargs["max_tool_calling_iterations"] = resolve_max_turns(t.get("env_config"))
147	        if self._use_vllm:
148	            kwargs["use_vllm"] = True
149	            kwargs["vllm_mode"] = "colocate"
150	            kwargs["vllm_gpu_memory_utilization"] = float(
151	                self.config["model"].get("gpu_memory_utilization", 0.3)
152	            )
153	            # Cap vLLM's context to the training seq length. Qwen3's native 40k
154	            # context would demand a ~4 GiB KV cache and OOM the colocated engine.
155	            kwargs["vllm_max_model_length"] = self._max_seq
156	            # TRL 1.6's default correction for the vLLM-vs-trainer logprob
157	            # mismatch is sequence_mask: the per-EPISODE weight exp(sum of
158	            # per-token drift) multiplies the loss, and a weight outside
159	            # [0, 3.0] is zeroed. The summed drift grows with completion
160	            # length, so long episodes lose their gradient preferentially
161	            # (ISR mean 0.28 on browsergym, 0.49 on poly - see
162	            # docs/plans/no-arm-beats-e0-audit.md). Configs name the mode
163	            # explicitly; "off" disables the correction, the four TRL mode
164	            # names pass through, absent keeps TRL's default so pre-fix
165	            # frozen configs retain their recorded semantics.
166	            is_mode = t.get("vllm_importance_sampling_mode")
167	            if is_mode == "off":
168	                kwargs["vllm_importance_sampling_correction"] = False
169	            elif is_mode is not None:
170	                kwargs["vllm_importance_sampling_mode"] = str(is_mode)
171	            print(f"vLLM importance sampling mode: "
172	                  f"{is_mode if is_mode is not None else 'sequence_mask (TRL default)'}")
173	        return GRPOConfig(**kwargs)
174	
175	    def train(self, dataset, reward_fn, output_dir: str, callbacks=None,
176	              *, server=None, make_factory=None) -> None:
177	        # Agentic path: the runner owns the env-server subprocess lifecycle.
178	        # `server` is an unstarted EnvServerProcess; once it is up, build the
179	        # TRL environment_factory against its base_url. Dataset path: both stay
180	        # None and the trainer runs without environments.
181	        environment_factory = None
182	        if server is not None:
183	            if make_factory is None:
184	                raise ValueError("train(server=...) requires make_factory(base_url)")
185	            # environment_factory is an experimental TRL feature; silence its warn.
186	            os.environ.setdefault("TRL_EXPERIMENTAL_SILENCE", "1")
187	            server.start()
188	            server.wait_until_ready()
189	            # The env client (adapter._connect) imports `reasoning_gym_env` from
190	            # the OpenEnv repo's envs/ dir, which is not on PyPI - put it on the
191	            # training process's path (the server subprocess got it via PYTHONPATH).
192	            if server.repo_envs_path not in sys.path:
193	                sys.path.insert(0, server.repo_envs_path)
194	            environment_factory = make_factory(server.base_url)
195	        try:
196	            kwargs = dict(
197	                model=self.model,
198	                processing_class=self.tokenizer,
199	                reward_funcs=[reward_fn],
200	                args=self._grpo_config(output_dir),
201	                train_dataset=dataset,
202	                callbacks=callbacks or [],
203	            )
204	            if environment_factory is not None:
205	                kwargs["environment_factory"] = environment_factory
206	            trainer = GRPOTrainer(**kwargs)
207	            trainer.train()
208	            self._save_train_log(trainer, output_dir)
209	        finally:
210	            if server is not None:
211	                server.stop()
212	
213	    def save_lora(self, path: str) -> None:
214	        self.model.save_pretrained(path)
215	        self.tokenizer.save_pretrained(path)
216	        print(f"LoRA saved to {path}")
217	
218	    @staticmethod
219	    def _save_train_log(trainer, output_dir: str) -> None:
220	        """Persist TRL's in-memory log_history to train_log.json.
221	
222	        TRL writes a checkpoint every `save_steps` (100 by default, since
223	        GRPOConfig's save_strategy is STEPS), but those carry only what the
224	        trainer needs to resume. The per-step curves - reward/kl/loss/completion
225	        length plus the per-component reward metrics the callback merged in -
226	        live in `state.log_history` and would vanish on exit. Dump them so
227	        eval.plots can draw training curves.
228	
229	        This runs after `trainer.train()` returns, so a killed run loses the
230	        file; its curves survive only as text in the batch log.
231	        """
232	        log = getattr(getattr(trainer, "state", None), "log_history", None)
233	        if not log:
234	            return
235	        path = os.path.join(output_dir, "train_log.json")
236	        with open(path, "w") as f:
237	            json.dump(log, f, indent=2)
238	        print(f"Training log saved to {path}")

This exists because the e27 run on disk is not usable as their baseline. Its frozen config records no batch_size key, it ran 2026-08-05, and the default was 1 until a19b1ff (2026-08-06) - train_log confirms it directly, epoch 0.6 at step 300 over a 500-question set is one prompt-group per optimizer step, and 47% of those steps had zero within-group reward variance and therefore no gradient. Comparing a bs=4 treatment arm against it would mix the reward's effect with 4x the prompts and roughly twice the live updates, which is the confound that voided every treatment-versus-baseline pair before a19b1ff. Geometry: 150 steps at batch_size 4 is 600 prompts and 150 optimizer updates against e27's 300 prompts and ~160 live updates - the same number of real gradient steps on twice the data, at ~365 s/it (interpolated from 94 s/it at bs=1 and 712 s/it at bs=8 on this env, both measured, both ~11.4 s per completion). 300 steps would double that to ~30h of training per arm and 4 days for the three; the box is shared and a run has already been handed away mid-campaign once. Everything else is e27 unchanged: same task mix, seed, budget, learning rate, composer and eval splits. naive_sum matches the E3 sweep so lambda=0 is the same code path.           f'clip mean {st.mean(clip) if clip else float("nan"):.4f}')

import json, statistics as st, math

    diffs = [b1b[s] - other[s] for s in common]

for fam, name in [(0, 'menu-2'), (1, 'dialog-2')]:
    for src, lab in [(b1b_r, '5e-5'), (b1_r, '2e-5'), (vf_r, '5e-6')]:

        for s, recs in src.items():

        first = st.mean([x for s in sorted(rews)[:25] for x in rews[s]])
