1	# BrowserGym difficulty: correction to the feasibility findings
2	
3	`browsergym_feasibility_findings.md` selected the e27 task mix from a probe whose
4	numbers do not transfer. This records what replaced them, and a hardware ceiling
5	that the corrected numbers exposed.
6	
7	Everything below was measured base-model, greedy, through `eval.runner
8	--base-model`, which drives the same `BrowserGymEnvAdapter` and prompt that
9	training uses. Twenty episodes per family, paired seeds (`seed_offset: 300000`)
10	across all three probes, so any family can be compared against itself between
11	budgets.
12	
13	## What went wrong with the original probe
14	
15	`pipeline/probes/bg_probe.py` built its tool list from `_BROWSERGYM_TOOLS` - all
16	five browsergym actions - and used its own prompt. The adapter exposes exactly
17	two, `click` and `noop`, and the domain supplies its own lead-in. Difficulty
18	measured under a five-tool menu does not survive contact with a two-tool one:
19	every family the two probes share came in about 0.45 higher under the real
20	conditions.
21	
22	| family | original probe | e27probe (real adapter) |
23	|---|---|---|
24	| click-option | 0.50 | 1.00 |
25	| click-checkboxes | 0.35 | 0.95 |
26	| click-widget | 0.60 | 0.90 |
27	| navigate-tree | 0.70 | 0.80 |
28	
29	e27 was launched on the left column and killed at step 21 of 300 with
30	`frac_reward_zero_std` 0.70 - 14 of 20 prompt groups had all 8 rollouts score
31	identically - and a mean reward of 0.931. No gradient, and worse, success and
32	termination had collapsed onto one axis, which is the condition the task set was
33	chosen to avoid.
34	
35	The lesson generalises past this bug: a difficulty number is only valid under
36	the tool surface, prompt, and token budget it was measured with. Two of those
37	three have now each invalidated a measurement in this project.
38	
39	## The prompt hint was not the cause
40	
41	The domain's `_LEAD_IN` ended "Most tasks need a selection followed by clicking
42	Submit", which is the solution to both training families stated outright. e27probe2
43	removed that sentence and changed nothing on paired seeds: click-option 1.00 ->
44	1.00, click-checkboxes 0.95 -> 1.00. The two-tool surface accounts for the
45	inflation on its own. The hint-free lead-in stays - handing over the plan is not
46	a fair measurement - but it is not a fix.
47	
48	## Half the difficulty ranking was truncation
49	
50	At a 2048-token budget the hard end of the ranking was mostly episodes cut off
51	mid-generation, not episodes that failed. e27probe3 re-ran the four survivors at
52	4096 on the same seeds.
53	
54	| family | acc 2048 -> 4096 | term 2048 -> 4096 | gap | cap-hits |
55	|---|---|---|---|---|
56	| navigate-tree | 0.80 -> 0.85 | 0.95 -> 0.85 | 0.15 -> 0.00 | 0 -> 0 |
57	| click-checkboxes-soft | 0.75 -> 0.85 | 0.80 -> 0.90 | 0.05 -> 0.05 | 3 -> 2 |
58	| click-checkboxes-large | 0.45 -> 0.60 | 0.45 -> 0.75 | 0.00 -> 0.15 | 8 -> 1 |
59	| click-tab-2 | 0.10 -> 0.05 | 0.35 -> 0.35 | 0.25 -> 0.30 | 11 -> 2 |
60	
61	click-checkboxes-large is the only family that clears both selection bars, and
62	it clears them only after the budget stops lying: five of the six seeds that
63	flipped to correct had stopped on `hit_generation_cap` at 2048. The mechanism is
64	attributed per seed, not inferred from the aggregate.
65	
66	click-tab-2 is the counter-example that keeps this from being "a bigger budget
67	lifts everything". Its cap-hits fell 11 -> 2 and its accuracy did not move,
68	because the freed budget went into looping instead: 5 of 20 episodes now run to
69	`max_turns` and 6 stop without calling a tool. It stays disqualified, at 0.05
70	success and a 5327-token median.
71	
72	navigate-tree moves the other way. Its 0.15 gap at 2048 was itself truncation;
73	at 4096 it reads 0.85 success against 0.85 termination, with all 17 terminated
74	episodes correct. Fully collapsed axes.
75	
76	### How much of this is noise
77	
78	The controls moved too, which needs accounting for. Comparing trajectories per
79	seed between the two budgets:
80	
81	| family | mean steps | identical trajectories | net accuracy change |
82	|---|---|---|---|
83	| navigate-tree | 1.6 | 16/20 | +1 episode |
84	| click-checkboxes-soft | 3.6 | 9/20 | +2 episodes |
85	| click-checkboxes-large | 5.9 | 3/20 | +3 episodes |
86	
87	Greedy decoding on a fixed seed should reproduce exactly, so the non-identical
88	trajectories are environment nondeterminism, and it compounds with episode
89	length - once one turn diverges, every later turn does. That sets a noise floor
90	of roughly one episode (0.05) on short families and more on long ones. It is a
91	standing limit on every 20-episode browsergym point estimate here, and it argues
92	for more episodes per family, not more families, in any future probe.
93	
94	click-checkboxes-large's termination moved 6 episodes with the mechanism visible
95	in the stop reasons, which is well clear of that floor. Its accuracy moved 3.
96	
97	## Why the winning family cannot be trained on this box
98	
99	TRL applies `max_completion_length` to the entire multi-turn trajectory rather
100	than per turn. `grpo_trainer.py:1605` drops tool results once `len(pct) -
101	len(prompt_ids[i])` passes it, and the loss at `grpo_trainer.py:2628` divides by
102	it, so the logits tensor is sized to it and memory scales with it directly. With
103	the fp32 logits upcast at roughly 10 bytes per token per vocabulary entry and a
104	151,936-entry vocabulary, 4096 completion tokens costs about 6.2 GB and 8192
105	about 12.5 GB, against the roughly 12 GB left on a 24 GB L4 after the policy and
106	the vLLM engine.
107	
108	Measured against that ceiling, using assistant tokens alone as a lower bound on
109	trajectory length (page observations count against the same budget on top):
110	
111	| family | median assistant tokens | episodes over 4096 |
112	|---|---|---|
113	| click-checkboxes-large | 6066 | 16/20 |
114	| click-checkboxes-soft | 3390 | 9/20 |
115	| navigate-tree | 331 | 3/20 |
116	
117	So click-checkboxes-large would train truncated in 16 of 20 episodes. That is
118	the e9-e21 artifact again, moved from the eval side to the training side, and it
119	would be harder to detect there.
120	
121	Across every family probed so far, difficulty and trajectory length are
122	entangled: the trainable ones are saturated, and the interesting one is too
123	long. Qwen3's thinking blocks are the proximate cause - about 1030 tokens per
124	turn on click-checkboxes-large, with every prior turn's block retained in the
125	completion. Turning thinking off is not the cheap way out: the model then emits
126	around 24 tokens and passes the visible label instead of the element id.
127	
128	## Greedy difficulty is not sampled difficulty
129	
130	The mix chosen above was launched and the discrepancy showed up in the first six
131	training steps. click-menu-2, probed at 0.60, ran near 0.10 per rollout;
132	click-dialog-2, probed at 0.80, ran near 0.875. Tool failure frequency was 0 and
133	completion lengths matched the probe, so neither a broken tool nor truncation
134	explains it.
135	
136	The probes ran greedy (`eval.temperature: 0.0`, `do_sample: false`). Training
137	samples at temperature 1.0 (`grpo_runner.py:93`, unset in the config so it takes
138	the default). GRPO's within-group variance - the thing the 0.40-0.80 band exists
139	to protect - depends on the sampled success rate, not the greedy one, and for a
140	2.6-step task the two differ by about 6x because each turn resamples an element
141	id and the errors compound.
142	
143	So a selection probe has to run `do_sample: true` at the training temperature.
144	Greedy accuracy answers "can the model do this task at all", which is the wrong
145	question for choosing a GRPO training set; the right one is "how often do eight
146	sampled rollouts disagree".
147	
148	A re-probe of these two families under sampling was queued and then dropped as
149	redundant, which is worth recording so nobody runs it. e27's own first steps
150	measure exactly what it would: the policy has barely moved after six steps, so
151	those per-rollout rates are the base sampled rates, and they are the 0.10 and
152	0.875 above. Spending two GPU-hours to re-derive a number the training log
153	already contains would delay the arms that need the GPU. The rule stands for
154	selecting a *new* family; it does not require re-measuring one already trained
155	on.
156	
157	This is the third instance of one error in this environment: difficulty measured
158	under conditions the training run does not use. The tool surface was first (five
159	tools versus two), the token budget second (2048 per turn versus 2048 for a
160	whole trajectory), and the decoding mode third. Each was invisible until
161	something downstream behaved impossibly.
162	
163	It did not sink the run - the policy learned anyway, reward climbing 0.375 to
164	0.734 over the first 30 steps - but that is luck rather than method. Had
165	click-dialog-2 not been in the mix, every group would have been all-zero and the
166	run would have had no gradient at all, which is exactly how finqa failed.
167	
168	## Train/eval budget mismatch
169	
170	Independently of which family wins, `max_seq - max_prompt_length` currently
171	feeds two different quantities: TRL's whole-trajectory `max_completion_length`
172	in training (`grpo_runner.py:78`), and `max_new_tokens` per turn in eval
173	(`agentic_eval.py:36`, where generate is called once per turn with no total
174	cap). On a single-turn domain these coincide, which is why reasoning_gym never
175	exposed it. On an n-turn domain they differ by a factor of n: e27's original
176	geometry gave training 2048 tokens for an entire 8-turn episode while eval
177	allowed 2048 on every turn. `eval.max_new_tokens` already overrides the eval
178	side, so the two can be set apart without a code change.
179	
180	## The competence boundary is about three decisions
181	
182	e27probe4 probed seven click-only families chosen to be decided in one or two
183	clicks. All seven:
184	
185	| family | acc | term | gap | median assistant tokens | steps |
186	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
187	| click-checkboxes-transfer | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 687 | 1.9 |
188	| click-dialog-2 | 0.80 | 1.00 | 0.20 | 385 | 1.0 |
189	| click-menu-2 | 0.60 | 0.70 | 0.10 | 2569 | 2.6 |
190	| grid-coordinate | 0.10 | 0.50 | 0.40 | 5904 | 3.4 |
191	| click-tab-2-hard | 0.10 | 0.20 | 0.10 | 6550 | 5.7 |
192	| click-collapsible-2 | 0.05 | 0.30 | 0.25 | 5638 | 4.8 |
193	| click-pie | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 8929 | 6.3 |
194	
195	The split is sharp and it falls on episode length, not on task family. At or
196	under 2.6 mean steps everything is solvable; at 3.4 and above everything is
197	dead, and always the same way - 5, 7, 10 and 13 of 20 episodes loop until
198	`max_turns`. Nothing sits in between.
199	
200	Fifteen families have now been measured under the real adapter. click-menu-2 and
201	click-dialog-2 are the only two that are both unsaturated and trainable, and
202	they became the e27 mix.
203	
204	Observation cost was measured through the real adapter rather than estimated
205	from the `_MAX_OBS_CHARS` cap: **45 tokens for a click-menu-2 page and 101 for
206	click-dialog-2**, against the roughly 500 a 2000-character cap implies. That
207	tenfold difference is what makes click-menu-2 trainable - its worst-case
208	trajectory lands near 4124 tokens rather than the 5107 the cap-based estimate
209	gave, so it fits a 4096 completion budget where the estimate said it could not.
210	A cap is an upper bound on a page, not the size of one.
211	
212	That explains why difficulty and trajectory length looked entangled in every
213	earlier probe: they are the same variable. Qwen3-1.7B does not fail MiniWoB
214	families because their pages are harder to read, it fails them once the episode
215	needs more steps than it can keep coherent, and a failing episode then spends
216	the entire remaining budget looping. The apparent difficulty of
217	click-checkboxes-large, click-tab-2, click-pie and click-collapsible-2 is one
218	phenomenon with one cause.
219	
220	The practical consequence is that the 0.40-0.80 band and the token budget are
221	not two independent bars for this model. Anything hard enough to be interesting
222	by looping its way there is untrainable by construction, so the only usable
223	families are the ones that are hard within two or three decisions.
224	
225	## Where this leaves the environment choice
226	
227	Three ways forward, in the order they should be tried:
228	
229	1. **Find a short-hard family.** e27probe4 probes seven click-only families
230	   decided in one or two clicks, where difficulty comes from reading the page
231	   rather than acting many times: click-pie, click-menu-2, click-collapsible-2,
232	   click-dialog-2, click-tab-2-hard, grid-coordinate, click-checkboxes-transfer.
233	   A third selection bar applies - median assistant tokens low enough that the
234	   trajectory and its observations fit 4096. Costs about two hours and needs no
235	   new code.
236	2. **Lift the completion ceiling.** A chunked or fused GRPO loss (Liger, already
237	   in BACKLOG) removes the fp32 logits materialisation and would make
238	   click-checkboxes-large trainable at its natural length. This is the only
239	   option that rescues the family already known to clear both bars.
240	3. **Shorten the trajectories.** Stripping prior turns' thinking blocks from the
241	   running completion would cut length by roughly the number of turns. It is a
242	   change to TRL's multi-turn loop and would alter what the policy conditions
243	   on, so it needs its own justification rather than being slipped in as an
244	   optimisation.
245	
246	Families excluded throughout, on the rule established for click-shape and
247	click-color: count-shape, count-sides, identify-shape and click-shades turn on
248	attributes an accessibility tree does not carry, so a text-only observation
249	cannot see the target at all.
250	
251	## Reproducing
252	
253	```
254	python -m eval.runner --config configs/e27probe-browsergym-difficulty-qwen3-1_7b.yaml --base-model
255	python -m eval.runner --config configs/e27probe2-browsergym-nohint-qwen3-1_7b.yaml --base-model
256	python -m eval.runner --config configs/e27probe3-browsergym-4k-qwen3-1_7b.yaml --base-model
257	python -m eval.runner --config configs/e27probe4-browsergym-short-qwen3-1_7b.yaml --base-model
258	```
259	
260	Per-episode records, including `stop_reason` and the ordered tool calls each
261	claim above rests on, are in `episodes_<split>.jsonl` under each run directory.
262

experiment_id: e30-browsergym-e1-menu-qwen3-1_7b
description: "E1 on the fixed trainer: task-success-only GRPO on click-menu-2 alone, the gate run of the Phase 5 campaign re-run (docs/plans/no-arm-beats-e0-audit.md). Three settled decisions meet here. (1) Trainer: e27bs4/e28bs4/e29bs4 trained under TRL's default sequence_mask importance-sampling filter, which suppressed exactly the long-completion gradient menu-2 emits (run-mean ISR 0.28); this run sets vllm_importance_sampling_mode: token_truncate, the fix verified by the 50-step probe ladder. (2) Learning rate: 5e-5, the top of a monotone same-seed dose-response (0.703 / 0.749 / 0.784 paired mean reward for 5e-6 / 2e-5 / 5e-5, no instability: grad_norm flat, KL 0.051 at 50 steps under kl_beta 0.001), and the ~10x-full-FT heuristic for LoRA. Temperature stays at the 1.0 default: 1.2 was probed and came out 2.2 SE below 1.0. (3) Task set (the C4 decision, 2026-08-13): click-dialog-2 leaves the training mix because it sits at or above the 40-80 band under sampling (~0.875 per rollout), contributes near-dead prompt groups, and diluted menu-2's gradient - the menu-only probe b3 was the first run of the audit whose within-run reward slope is positive (0.588 to 0.756 over 50 steps). No replacement family joins: of the fifteen probed under the real adapter, the only mid-band one (click-checkboxes-large, 0.60 at a 4096 budget) has a 6066-token median trajectory that would train truncated in 16 of 20 episodes on this box, and every other family is saturated or dead-by-looping (browsergym_difficulty_correction.md). Geometry: batch_size 4 / n_rollouts 8 / 150 steps, identical to the e27bs4 campaign; menu-only runs ~430 s/it measured on the b3 probe, so ~18h of training. Gate protocol: this run must beat the paired base model (e0m-browsergym-base-menu, identical splits and seeds, no adapter) on training-reward slope plus paired held-out eval before the E2/E3 arms are trained on top of the recipe. Power (plan item E, fixed before launch): held_out n=200 for the paired McNemar read (~10-15pt detectable at the observed discordance), shifted n=150 across three untrained families - click-dialog-2 now among them, so the shifted split reads substitution in both directions, not degradation only. The training log (4800 episodes) remains the stronger continuous readout for the slope half of the gate."
seed: 42

model:
  slug: qwen3-1.7b
  # Initial prompt is small (lead-in, goal, first page: about 700 tokens), and
  # the whole trajectory is capped at 4096 below, so 8192 leaves slack.
  max_seq_length: 8192
  lora_r: 16
  gpu_memory_utilization: 0.30

training:
  mode: agentic
  env: browsergym
  env_config:
    benchmark: miniwob
    # Menu-only (C4): every seed maps to click-menu-2, so the whole batch is
    # the one family with headroom. Even seeds produce the same questions the
    # mixed e27bs4 campaign drew for menu, odd seeds are new menu questions.
    tasks: [click-menu-2]
    # MiniWoB HTML is not shipped with browsergym-miniwob. This must point at a
    # served clone of miniwob-plusplus or the env raises "core is not defined"
    # at the first reset, and it does not survive a box restart. Start it first:
    #   cd /workspace/miniwob-plusplus/miniwob/html && python3 -m http.server 8080
    miniwob_url: http://localhost:8080/miniwob/
    # The one turn cap. Menu-2 needs 2.6 steps, so 8 is headroom.
    max_turns: 8
  env_server:
    repo_path: /workspace/OpenEnv/envs
    port: 8000
  # Sets TRL's max_completion_length to 8192 - 4096 = 4096, the budget for the
  # WHOLE trajectory. Menu-2's worst case lands near 4124 tokens (45-token
  # pages measured through the adapter), so truncation stays rare.
  max_prompt_length: 4096
  # Geometry stated explicitly so the frozen config records it. Every arm built
  # on this recipe must carry these three keys identically or the frozen-config
  # diff cannot prove a single-knob comparison.
  batch_size: 4
  n_rollouts: 8
  micro_batch_size: 1
  max_steps: 150
  # 10x the e27bs4 campaign's 5e-6: top of the probe ladder's monotone
  # dose-response, stable at 50 steps. Watch KL growth past that horizon.
  learning_rate: 5e-5
  kl_beta: 0.001
  # The trainer fix (commit a975c40). The TRL 1.6 default, sequence_mask,
  # zeroes or collapses the per-sequence weight of long completions and starved
  # menu-2 of gradient in every earlier browsergym run.
  vllm_importance_sampling_mode: token_truncate

rewards:
  # Matches the future E3 arm's composer so lambda=0 is the same code path.
  compose_method: naive_sum
  env_reward:
    enabled: true
    weight: 1.0

eval:
  temperature: 0.0
  do_sample: false
  # Pinned, not derived. Budget for the WHOLE trajectory, matching TRL's
  # max_completion_length in training. Every arm of the campaign must state the
  # same value or the comparison is measured under two different budgets.
  max_new_tokens: 4096
  # Thinking rates are measured against the paired base model's token
  # distribution, not this run's own percentiles, so every arm of the campaign
  # is scored on one ruler. e0m must therefore be evaluated first.
  reference_report: runs/e0m-browsergym-base-menu-qwen3-1_7b/eval_report.json
  agentic:
    splits:
      # Held-out: menu-2 questions from this seed's block, disjoint from the
      # training seeds via the offset. n=200 per the power plan in the
      # description.
      - name: held_out
        n_episodes: 200
      # Shifted: three families never trained on. click-dialog-2 (base 0.80)
      # detects substitution in both directions; navigate-tree and
      # click-checkboxes-transfer (at ceiling) detect degradation. 50 episodes
      # per family via seed % 3.
      - name: shifted
        n_episodes: 150
        env_config:
          tasks: [click-dialog-2, navigate-tree, click-checkboxes-transfer]
        seed_offset: 200000

#!/bin/bash
# Monitor phase 1 of the e30 gate: the e0m base eval (pid 1752886 script).
# Exits (-> task notification) on: phase boundary ("e0m done"), abort, or pid gone.
# Tolerates tunnel flaps with deduped state-change messages.
RUN=/workspace/master-thesis-code/pipeline/runs/e0m-browsergym-base-menu-qwen3-1_7b
LOG=/workspace/e30_gate.log
PID=1752886
last_state=up
last_mile=""
while true; do
  out=$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=15 -o BatchMode=yes gpu-l4 "
    if kill -0 $PID 2>/dev/null; then alive=1; else alive=0; fi
    ho=\$(wc -l < $RUN/episodes_held_out.jsonl 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    sh=\$(wc -l < $RUN/episodes_shifted.jsonl 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    done_line=\$(grep -c 'e0m done rc=' $LOG 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    abort=\$(grep -c 'GATE ABORT' $LOG 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    err=\$(grep -ciE 'traceback|CUDA out of memory|RuntimeError' $LOG 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    echo \"STATE alive=\$alive held=\$ho shifted=\$sh done=\$done_line abort=\$abort err=\$err\"
  " 2>/dev/null | grep '^STATE')
  if [ -z "$out" ]; then
    if [ "$last_state" = "up" ]; then echo "BOX-UNREACHABLE $(date -u +%H:%M)"; last_state=down; fi
    sleep 300; continue
  fi
  if [ "$last_state" = "down" ]; then echo "TUNNEL-BACK $(date -u +%H:%M)"; last_state=up; fi
  alive=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*alive=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  held=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*held=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  shifted=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*shifted=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  donec=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*done=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  abort=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*abort=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  err=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*err=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  if [ "$abort" -gt 0 ]; then echo "E0M-ABORT held=$held shifted=$shifted"; exit 0; fi
  if [ "$donec" -gt 0 ]; then echo "E0M-DONE held=$held shifted=$shifted -> e30 train phase starting"; exit 0; fi
  if [ "$alive" = "0" ]; then echo "GATE-DIED held=$held shifted=$shifted err=$err"; exit 0; fi
  mile="h$((held / 25))s$((shifted / 25))"
  if [ "$mile" != "$last_mile" ]; then
    echo "E0M-PROGRESS held_out $held/200 shifted $shifted/150 err=$err $(date -u +%H:%M)"
    last_mile=$mile
  fi
  sleep 300
done

Running now on the box (launched 12:14 UTC, pid 1752886, commit `528098f`), three phases chained:

1. **e0m base eval** - the paired E0 reference on the new menu-only splits (held_out n=200, shifted n=150 across dialog-2 / navigate-tree / checkboxes-transfer). Runs first because e30 pins its thinking thresholds to this report. ETA ~20:00 UTC today.

## 3. Model scale x quantization sweep - larger Qwen3, 4-bit where needed

Supersedes the audit plan's D1, which was gated on "menu-2 stays flat" and
deleted when B3 refuted that premise. This is the ungated version: parameter
count and quantization are exploration axes in their own right - try the next
larger Qwen3 rung(s), quantized where bf16 does not fit the 24 GB L4.

Registry state today: the `qwen3-4b` slug points at `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Base`,
which is the wrong lineage counterpart - the pipeline's 1.7B is the
post-trained `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` with the tool-calling chat template. A 4B rung
needs a `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` entry; an 8B rung needs a new entry with
`load_in_4bit: true` (bf16 8B is ~16 GB of weights before the vLLM colocate
copy and the logits path). Eval-only probes (HF greedy generate, no vLLM) fit
4B in bf16 easily; 4B training likely needs 4-bit or tightened budgets.

Method constraints, so the sweep produces comparable numbers:

- The difficulty band is model-relative. menu-2 at ~0.59 sampled for 1.7B may
  saturate for 4B, and families dead-by-looping for 1.7B (checkboxes-large,
  tab-2) may become trainable - the C4 elimination does not transfer, so the
  candidate pool reopens per model. Re-run the band check sampled at the
  training temperature before training any new scale.
- Quantization is a treatment, not free memory. Hold it fixed within any
  compared pair; a 4-bit arm against a bf16 arm confounds scale with precision.
- Each scale gets its own e0 base eval on identical splits before its E1.
- QLoRA + vLLM colocate has an open correctness question: if vLLM serves a
  bf16 copy while the trainer computes on nf4 weights, sampler and trainer
  diverge systematically per token - the same length-correlated drift the TIS
  audit just closed. Before training quantized, check what precision the vLLM
  copy runs at and confirm ISR stays ~1.0 under `token_truncate`.

Steps: fix the registry entries, D1-style base eval of 4B on the e0m splits
(cheap, eval-only, answers "does scale alone move menu-2"), then decide
whether a trained 4B arm is worth the geometry re-run.

#!/bin/bash
# Monitor phase 2 of the e30 gate: training (150 steps, pid 1809005).
# Exits (-> task notification) when training stops running (transition to eval
# OR death - differentiated after exit), on abort, or on batch-done.
LOG=/workspace/master-thesis-code/pipeline/runs/e30-browsergym-e1-menu-qwen3-1_7b/batch_train.log
GLOG=/workspace/e30_gate.log
last_state=up
last_mile=""
while true; do
  out=$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=15 -o BatchMode=yes gpu-l4 "
    if pgrep -f 'training.train --config configs/e30' > /dev/null 2>&1; then alive=1; else alive=0; fi
    steps=\$(grep -c \"'loss'\" $LOG 2>/dev/null; true)
    err=\$(grep -ciE 'traceback|CUDA out of memory' $LOG 2>/dev/null; true)
    bdone=\$(grep -c 'e30 batch done' $GLOG 2>/dev/null; true)
    echo \"STATE alive=\${alive} steps=\${steps:-0} err=\${err:-0} bdone=\${bdone:-0}\"
  " 2>/dev/null | grep '^STATE' | head -1)
  if [ -z "$out" ]; then
    if [ "$last_state" = "up" ]; then echo "BOX-UNREACHABLE $(date -u +%H:%M)"; last_state=down; fi
    sleep 600; continue
  fi
  if [ "$last_state" = "down" ]; then echo "TUNNEL-BACK $(date -u +%H:%M)"; last_state=up; fi
  alive=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*alive=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  steps=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*steps=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  err=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*err=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  bdone=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*bdone=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  case "$alive$steps$err$bdone" in *[!0-9]*) echo "PARSE-ODD: $out"; sleep 600; continue;; esac
  if [ "$bdone" -gt 0 ]; then echo "E30-BATCH-DONE steps=$steps"; exit 0; fi
  if [ "$alive" = "0" ]; then echo "E30-TRAIN-STOPPED steps=$steps err=$err (eval transition or death - check gate log)"; exit 0; fi
  mile=$((steps / 10))
  if [ "$mile" != "$last_mile" ]; then
    echo "E30-TRAIN-PROGRESS step $steps/150 err=$err $(date -u +%H:%M)"
    last_mile=$mile
  fi
  sleep 600
done

while true; do

  if [ -z "$out" ]; then
    if [ "$last_state" = "up" ]; then echo "BOX-UNREACHABLE $(date -u +%H:%M)"; last_state=down; fi

  fi
  if [ "$last_state" = "down" ]; then echo "TUNNEL-BACK $(date -u +%H:%M)"; last_state=up; fi
  alive=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*alive=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  bdone=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*bdone=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  rep=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*rep=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  eps=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*eps=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  case "$alive$bdone$rep$eps" in *[!0-9]*) echo "PARSE-ODD: $out"; sleep 300; continue;; esac
  if [ "$bdone" -gt 0 ]; then echo "E30-BATCH-DONE eps=$eps rep=$rep"; exit 0; fi
  if [ "$alive" = "0" ]; then echo "E30-EVAL-STOPPED eps=$eps rep=$rep (done or death - check gate log)"; exit 0; fi
  echo "E30-EVAL-PROGRESS shifted $eps/150 $(date -u +%H:%M)"
  sleep 300
done

input.content:
# e30 gate: E1 (menu-only, fixed trainer) vs e0m base - PASSED

Date: 2026-08-14. Runs: `e0m-browsergym-base-menu-qwen3-1_7b` (base model,
no adapter) and `e30-browsergym-e1-menu-qwen3-1_7b` (task-success-only GRPO,
click-menu-2, 150 steps, lr 5e-5, `token_truncate` ISR). Identical splits and
seeds; e30's thinking-rate thresholds pinned to e0m's report. Gate protocol
from `docs/plans/no-arm-beats-e0-audit.md`: e30 must beat e0m on training-reward
slope plus paired held-out eval before the E2/E3 arms run on the recipe.

## Verdict

Both halves pass, decisively. The first trained arm of the project that beats
its own base model - the "no arm beats e0" symptom is resolved by the recipe
(menu-only task set + 5e-5 + `token_truncate`), on one seed.

## Held-out (click-menu-2, n=200, paired seed-for-seed)

| | e0m | e30 |
|---|---|---|
| success | 0.595 [0.525, 0.661] | 1.000 [0.981, 1.000] |
| non-termination | 0.295 | 0.000 [0.000, 0.019] |
| mean tokens (correct eps) | 1908 | 1541 [1470, 1610] |
| mean steps | 3.09 | 2.61 |
| stop reasons | 141 env_done / 48 no_tool_call / 11 cap | 200 env_done |

- Discordant pairs: e30-only-correct 81, e0m-only-correct 0. Exact McNemar
  two-sided p = 8.3e-25. Zero regressions.
- On the 119 jointly-correct episodes: paired median token diff -643, paired
  mean -442.6, e30 shorter on 82/119. Compression is incidental - this arm has
  no length reward - and sets the bar E2 must beat to claim the cosine adds
  anything.

## Training slope (150 steps, buckets of 10)

reward 0.562 0.591 0.569 0.634 0.841 0.803 0.691 0.769 0.772 0.803 0.762
0.847 0.884 0.875 0.912. KL 0.001 -> 0.101 (settling, kl_beta 0.001);
grad_norm flat. Both mid-run watch-items resolved on their own: completion
mean length peaked at 2750 (bucket 4) and fell to 1818 by step 150;
trajectory-cap clipping peaked 0.19 and ended 0.016. frac_reward_zero_std
rose from ~0.5 to ~0.725 as the task saturated.

## Shifted (untrained families, n=50 each, paired)

| family | e0m acc | e30 acc | e0m term | e30 term | McNemar p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| click-dialog-2 | 0.780 | 0.600 | 1.000 | 0.740 | 0.064 |
| navigate-tree | 0.620 | 0.640 | 0.640 | 0.760 | 1.0 |
| click-checkboxes-transfer | 1.000 | 0.940 | 1.000 | 0.940 | 0.25 |

Suggestive substitution cost on click-dialog-2, not significant at n=50: the
trained arm stops terminating on the family it never saw (terminated 1.000 ->
0.740; 27 of the 28 shifted failures beyond the cap hit are no_tool_call).
This is the RQ2 substitution read the C4 decision moved dialog-2 to the
shifted split to expose, and it is the sharpest thing E3 can act on: the
non-termination penalty prices exactly this failure.

## Caveats for reading E2/E3 against e30

- Single seed (42), greedy eval. Nothing here is seed-replicated yet.
- Held-out accuracy is at ceiling. E2/E3 cannot beat 1.000 - the informative
  axes are token counts, training dynamics, and the shifted split.
- e30 ends with ~72% zero-std prompt groups. A length reward varies where env
  reward is constant, so the E2 arm will train on more live groups - check
  `frac_reward_zero_std` in both logs before attributing any difference to the
  reward's shape (the "reward plus more gradient" confound, CLAUDE.md).
- The e27bs4/e28bs4/e29bs4 numbers do not carry over: two-task mix, lr 5e-6,
  and the `sequence_mask` ISR filter (run-mean ISR 0.28) that starved long
  completions of gradient.

## Timing (L4)

e0m eval 3h50m (350 episodes). e30 train 19h30m (150 steps, ~492 s/it minus
startup), e30 eval 5h12m. Full gate 28h32m.

#!/bin/bash
# Monitor the e31+e32 batch (two train+eval runs, ~49h total).
# Milestones every 10 train steps, phase changes on run-dir contents.
# Exits (-> task notification) when the batch process dies (done or crash).
BLOG=/workspace/e31_e32_batch.log
R31=/workspace/master-thesis-code/pipeline/runs/e31-browsergym-e2-cosine-menu-qwen3-1_7b
R32=/workspace/master-thesis-code/pipeline/runs/e32-browsergym-e3-nontermination-menu-qwen3-1_7b
last_state=up
last_sig=""
while true; do
  out=$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=15 -o BatchMode=yes gpu-l4 "
    if ps aux | grep 'training.batch' | grep -v grep > /dev/null; then alive=1; else alive=0; fi
    s31=\$(grep -c \"'loss'\" $R31/batch_train.log 2>/dev/null; true)
    s32=\$(grep -c \"'loss'\" $R32/batch_train.log 2>/dev/null; true)
    r31=\$(ls $R31/eval_report.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    r32=\$(ls $R32/eval_report.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    err=\$(grep -ciE 'traceback|CUDA out of memory' $BLOG 2>/dev/null; true)
    echo \"STATE alive=\${alive} s31=\${s31:-0} s32=\${s32:-0} r31=\${r31} r32=\${r32} err=\${err:-0}\"
  " 2>/dev/null | grep '^STATE' | head -1)
  if [ -z "$out" ]; then
    if [ "$last_state" = "up" ]; then echo "BOX-UNREACHABLE $(date -u +%H:%M)"; last_state=down; fi
    sleep 900; continue
  fi
  if [ "$last_state" = "down" ]; then echo "TUNNEL-BACK $(date -u +%H:%M)"; last_state=up; fi
  alive=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*alive=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  s31=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*s31=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  s32=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*s32=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  r31=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*r31=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  r32=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*r32=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  err=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/.*err=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  case "$alive$s31$s32$r31$r32$err" in *[!0-9]*) echo "PARSE-ODD: $out"; sleep 900; continue;; esac
  if [ "$alive" = "0" ]; then echo "E31E32-BATCH-STOPPED s31=$s31 s32=$s32 r31=$r31 r32=$r32 err=$err (done or death - check batch log)"; exit 0; fi
  sig="$((s31 / 10)).$((s32 / 10)).$r31.$r32"
  if [ "$sig" != "$last_sig" ]; then
    echo "E31E32-PROGRESS e31: $s31/150 rep=$r31 | e32: $s32/150 rep=$r32 err=$err $(date -u +%H:%M)"
    last_sig=$sig
  fi
  sleep 900
done

content.text:
**Gate passed and the campaign's E2/E3 arms are now training.** Full picture:

**e30 result (the audit's payoff).** First trained arm in the whole project that beats its base model: held_out 0.595 -> 1.000 (n=200 paired, McNemar p=8.3e-25, 81 flips forward, zero backward). Non-termination 0.295 -> 0.000. And it compressed without any length reward: -643 tokens paired median on jointly-correct episodes. Training reward climbed 0.562 -> 0.912; both mid-run watch-items (length drift, clipping) resolved themselves in the second half.

**One finding to hold:** dialog-2 on the shifted split dropped 0.780 -> 0.600 (p=0.064, suggestive not significant) - the trained model stops terminating on the family it never saw. That is the RQ2 substitution signal, and it is exactly the failure the E3 penalty prices, which makes the e32 arm more interesting than expected.

**Ceiling caveat:** held_out accuracy is saturated at 1.000, so E2/E3 compare on tokens, training dynamics, and shifted behavior - not accuracy.

**Launched:** e31 (E2 cosine) + e32 (E3 non-termination), single-knob copies of e30 (verified key-level), one batch on the box. ETA: e31 done ~Aug 15 evening, e32 ~Aug 16 evening. Monitor up, findings in `pipeline/runs/e30_gate_findings.md`, commit d6d4c49.

Next steps:
- Monitor fires on batch progress/completion; e31 harvest + paired read vs e30 ~Aug 15 evening.
- After both arms: seed replication decision (42-only so far) and the frac_zero_std gradient-share check before any E2 claim.

import json, math, statistics
from collections import defaultdict

def load(run, split):
    p = f"pipeline/runs/{run}/episodes_{split}.jsonl"
    return {json.loads(l)["seed"]: json.loads(l) for l in open(p)}

E0="e0m-browsergym-base-menu-qwen3-1_7b"; E1="e30-browsergym-e1-menu-qwen3-1_7b"
E2="e31-browsergym-e2-cosine-menu-qwen3-1_7b"; E3="e32-browsergym-e3-nontermination-menu-qwen3-1_7b"

def mcnemar(a, b, seeds):
    x = sum(1 for s in seeds if a[s]["correct"] and not b[s]["correct"])
    y = sum(1 for s in seeds if not a[s]["correct"] and b[s]["correct"])
    n = x+y
    p = min(1.0, sum(math.comb(n,k) for k in range(min(x,y)+1)) / 2**(n-1)) if n else 1.0
    return x, y, p

print("== held_out paired vs e30 ==")
h = {r: load(r, "held_out") for r in [E0, E1, E2, E3]}
seeds = sorted(set(h[E1]) & set(h[E2]) & set(h[E3]))
for arm, name in [(E2,"e31 cosine"), (E3,"e32 non-term")]:
    x, y, p = mcnemar(h[E1], h[arm], seeds)
    both = [s for s in seeds if h[E1][s]["correct"] and h[arm][s]["correct"]]
    d = sorted(h[arm][s]["n_tokens"] - h[E1][s]["n_tokens"] for s in both)
    print(f"{name}: e30-only-correct={x} arm-only-correct={y} McNemar p={p:.3g}; "
          f"jointly-correct n={len(both)} paired median tok diff {d[len(d)//2]}, mean {statistics.mean(d):.0f}")
# also vs e0m
for arm, name in [(E2,"e31"), (E3,"e32")]:
    x, y, p = mcnemar(h[E0], h[arm], seeds)
    print(f"{name} vs e0m: e0m-only={x} arm-only={y} p={p:.3g}")

print("\n== shifted per family (acc / term) ==")
TASKS = ["click-dialog-2", "navigate-tree", "click-checkboxes-transfer"]
s = {r: load(r, "shifted") for r in [E0, E1, E2, E3]}
sseeds = sorted(set(s[E0]) & set(s[E1]) & set(s[E2]) & set(s[E3]))
for t in TASKS:
    fs = [x for x in sseeds if TASKS[x % 3] == t]
    row = f"{t}: "
    for r, nm in [(E0,"e0m"),(E1,"e30"),(E2,"e31"),(E3,"e32")]:
        acc = sum(s[r][x]["correct"] for x in fs)/len(fs)
        term = sum(s[r][x]["terminated"] for x in fs)/len(fs)
        row += f"{nm} {acc:.2f}/{term:.2f}  "
    print(row)
for t in TASKS:
    fs = [x for x in sseeds if TASKS[x % 3] == t]
    for arm, nm in [(E2,"e31"),(E3,"e32")]:
        x, y, p = mcnemar(s[E1], s[arm], fs)
        print(f"  {t} {nm} vs e30: {x}/{y} p={p:.3g}")

print("\n== e32 train slope ==")
rows = json.load(open(f"pipeline/runs/{E3}/train_log.json"))
if not isinstance(rows, list): rows = rows.get("log_history", rows)
def f(r,k):
    try: return float(r[k])
    except (KeyError,TypeError,ValueError): return None
steps=[r for r in rows if f(r,"reward") is not None]
comp=[k for k in steps[0] if "contrib" in k]
for key in ["reward","frac_reward_zero_std","kl","completions/mean_length"]+comp:
    vals=[f(r,key) for r in steps]; vals=[v for v in vals if v is not None]
    if not vals: continue
    b=[statistics.mean(vals[i:i+10]) for i in range(0,len(vals),10)]
    print(f"{key}: "+" ".join(f"{x:.3f}" for x in b))

# e31 (E2 cosine) and e32 (E3 non-termination) vs e30 (E1) - the campaign read

Date: 2026-08-16. Both arms are single-knob copies of e30 (verified by
key-level config diff): e31 adds `token_length` (cosine, w1.0, max_len 4096),
e32 adds `non_termination` (w1.0). Same seed (42), geometry, lr 5e-5,
`token_truncate`, splits, and e0m-pinned thinking thresholds. All paired
seed-for-seed; exact McNemar throughout. Single seed, greedy eval.

## Headline

Both efficiency rewards work as designed AND produce a measurable off-target
cost, in opposite directions. Both still beat the base model.

| held_out (menu-2, n=200) | e0m | e30 (E1) | e31 (E2) | e32 (E3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| success | 0.595 | 1.000 | 0.930 | 0.730 |
| mean tokens (correct) | 1908 | 1541 | 487 | 1400 |
| non-termination | 0.295 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

| shifted acc (n=50/family) | e0m | e30 | e31 | e32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| click-dialog-2 | 0.78 | 0.60 | 0.56 | **0.90** |
| navigate-tree | 0.62 | 0.64 | 0.74 | 0.70 |
| click-checkboxes-transfer | 1.00 | 0.94 | 0.98 | 0.92 |

## E2 (cosine): compression is real, and it buys some of it with correctness

- vs e30 held_out: 14 losses / 0 wins, p=1.2e-4. The 7pt drop is the Wu/Yeo
  overshoot, directly observed for the first time in this project.
- Compression is massive: paired median -1130 tokens on the 186
  jointly-correct episodes (487 vs 1541 mean; -68%). Underthinking rate 1.0 -
  every correct episode sits below e0m's P10. Training mean length 2257 ->
  643; train ran 13h vs e30's 19.5h because completions shrank.
- vs e0m: 67/0 flips, p=1.4e-20. Better AND 4x shorter than base.
- Shifted: no dialog-2 rescue (0.56, p=0.8 vs e30); navigate-tree up 0.64 ->
  0.74 (p=0.06, suggestive).
- Confounds to carry: `frac_reward_zero_std` = 0.000 every bucket (e30
  ~0.5-0.7) - the cosine gives every group live gradient, so E2 = "reward +
  more gradient", per the standing caveat. KL 0.368 vs e30's 0.101 - the
  policy moved 3.6x further; some of the 7pt may be drift, not the reward's
  length preference per se. env-component slope (0.544 -> 0.934) tracked
  e30's throughout, so task learning was not visibly starved during training.

## E3 (non-termination): transfers the intended behavior, taxes the task

- vs e30 held_out: 54 losses / 0 wins, p=1.1e-16. A 27pt cost on the trained
  family relative to task-reward-only. Still beats e0m (44/17, p=7.3e-4).
- The penalty's own target saturates fast: NonTerminationPenalty contrib_l1
  0.272 -> ~0.03 by bucket 5 - non-termination is trained away in the first
  ~50 steps, after which the component is nearly inert while env learning
  continues weaker than e30's (final env contrib 0.863 vs e30 reward 0.912).
- The striking result is shifted: dialog-2 0.90 vs e30's 0.60 (18/3 flips,
  p=1.5e-3) and above e0m's 0.78; terminated 0.98. The penalty prevented -
  and reversed - the substitution collapse E1 induced on the unseen family.
  Pooled shifted 0.840, best of all four arms. E3 appears to train "act and
  terminate" as a family-general behavior rather than menu-specific policy.
- RQ2's token-side prediction (buying termination with tokens) shows up as
  absence-of-compression: e32 length ends ~2165 vs e30's 1818, correct-ep
  tokens 1400 (vs 1541) - no compression beyond noise, unlike every other
  trained arm.

## What this means for the thesis

The three-arm contrast is exactly the RQ2 structure the study was built for:
task reward alone (E1) maximizes the trained family and quietly degrades an
unseen one; the length reward (E2) converts tokens into a small correctness
tax; the termination penalty (E3) trades trained-family headroom for
robustness of the terminate-behavior across families. One seed; none of this
is replicated yet.

## Caveats

- Single seed (42), greedy eval, one environment family trained.
- Held-out ceiling in e30 means E2/E3 could only tie or lose there by
  construction; the paired flip counts (14/0, 54/0) are the honest readout.
- e31's gradient-share and KL confounds above.
- e32's held-out drop conflates the penalty's effect with ~5% weaker env
  learning during training - a lambda sweep (0.25/0.5) would separate
  penalty-induced behavior change from gradient dilution.
- e0m's shifted dialog-2 (0.78) and the probe-era 0.875 differ by draw and
  temperature; comparisons here use the paired n=50 split only.

## Timing (L4)

e31 train 13.0h + eval 2.2h (short completions); e32 train 19.4h + eval
5.6h. Batch wall 40h35m (`batch_summary_20260816_092835.md`).
